[[File:Yodohime-jinja Haiden.jpg|thumb|right|''Yodohime jinja'']] {{nihongo|'''Yodohime jinja'''|與止日女神社|}}, also known as the '''Kawakami jinja''', is a [[Japan]]ese [[Shinto shrine]] in [[Saga, Saga|Saga]], [[Saga Prefecture]]. ==Overview== {{Shrine |Name = Yodohime Shrine |Image = [[File:Yodohime-jinja Haiden.jpg|270px]]
Shrine grounds |Location = [[Saga Prefecture]][[Saga City]] Yamatomachi Kawakami 1 |Position = {{WikiCoordinates2degrees|33|19|34.7|N|130|16|6|E|display=inline,title}} |Deity = Yodohime-no-Mikoto |Sacred Object = |Rank = [[Shikinai-sha]] (small)
[[Hizen Province]] [[Ichinomiya]]
Former [[Ken-sha]] |Founding = 25th year of Emperor Kinmei (564?) |Main Hall = Five-bay Nagare-zukuri |Alias = Kawakami Shrine, Yodohime-san |Pilgrimage = |Annual Festival = [[April 18]], [[December 18]] |Rituals = Autumn Festival (Okunchi, [[October 10]]) |Map = {{Location map|Japan Saga|label=Yodohime Shrine|position=bottom|width=200|float=center|caption=|mark=Shinto torii icon vermillion.svg|marksize=20}}{{maplink2|frame=yes|plain=yes|type=point|zoom=12|frame-align=center|frame-width=200}} }} {{Coordinates list}} [[File:Yodohime-jinja keidai.JPG|thumb|200px|right|Shrine grounds and [[Kase River]]]] [[File:Yodohime-jinja sannnotorii.JPG|thumb|200px|right|Third Torii (City-designated cultural property)
Hizen Torii.]] '''Yodohime Shrine''' (Yodohime-jinja, also known as '''Yodohime Shrine''') is a [[shrine]] located in [[Saga Prefecture]], [[Saga City]]. It is a [[Shikinai-sha]], [[Ichinomiya]] of [[Hizen Province]], and a former [[Ken-sha]] under the modern shrine ranking system. It is also written as "Yodohime Shrine" and is also known as "'''Kawakami Shrine'''" and colloquially as "Yodohime-san." == History == === Founding === According to a fragment from the '[[Hizen Province Fudoki]]' (Shinmyocho Tochu), the god Yodohime was enshrined on November 1 in the 25th year of Emperor Kinmei (564?). It is said that Ayu fish and other fish swam upstream and dived near the northern part of Setahime Shrine, suggesting it was established as a water god worship from a river-related legend recorded in the same book'Gods of Japan' Yodohime Shrine section. === Historical Overview === In the 5th year of [[Engi (era name)|Engi]] (927), the '[[Engishiki]]' [[Engishiki Jinmyocho|Jinmyocho]] lists "Yodohime Shrine" in [[Saga District]], Hizen Province, and it was included among the [[Shikinai-sha]]. In the first year of [[Kochou]] (1260), it was granted the highest rank of Shoichii (Senior First Rank). In the [[Heian period]], Tajima-no-Kami Shrine (present-day [[Tajima Shrine]]) was revered as the god of safe voyages in Hizen Province and was ranked higher than Yodohime Shrine in the 'Jinmyocho', being the only Omiya in Hizen Province. However, after the medieval period, the actual status of Yodohime Shrine, which was closer to the provincial office, rose, and it was revered as Hizen Province's Ichinomiya. In the years of [[Oho]] (1161-1163), it became the Ichinomiya of Hizen Province, and in the first year of Kochou (1261), it received the Shoichii rank. However, as mentioned later, [[Chikushi Hachiman Shrine]] also claims to be Ichinomiya. During the [[Mongol invasions of Japan]] (1281), it is said that the godly spirit of Yodohime-no-Mikoto destroyed the enemy ships. In the 7th year of [[Keicho]] (1602), Emperor Go-Yozei personally bestowed a plaque inscribed with "Great Guardian of Japan's Western Region, Hizen Province's Great Protector, Shoichii Yodohime Daimyojin Ichinomiya" (preserved in the main hall: not open to the public). This confirms that Yodohime Shrine was recognized as the Ichinomiya of Hizen Province, leading to a 60-year dispute with Chikushi Hachiman Shrine over the title. According to old records, the main hall, Heiden, and Haiden were burned down in the 10th year of Bunka (1813) and rebuilt by the Nabeshima family in the 13th year of Bunka (1816). In the 4th year of [[Meiji]] (1871), it was classified as a [[Ken-sha]] under the modern shrine ranking system. There were plans for its elevation to a Kokuheisha, but these were not realized due to the end of [[World War II]]. === Divine Rank === * Six National Histories ** [[Jogan (Japan)|Jogan]] 2nd year (860) February 8th, from Jugoi-no-ge to Jugoi-no-jo ( '[[Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku]]') - Written as "Yodohime Tenjin". ** Jogan 15th year (873) September 16th, Shogoi-no-ge ( 'Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku') - Written as "Yodohime no Kami". * Kochou first year (1260), Shoichii == Deities == * '''Yodohime-no-Mikoto''' *: Said to be the sister of [[Empress Jingu]]. Another theory states she is [[Toyotama-hime]]Deities according to the shrine's origin story.. *: In a fragment of the '[[Hizen Province Fudoki]]' (Shinmyocho Tochu), it is stated that the alternate names for "Yodohime no Kami" are "Toyohime" and "Yodohime". Another section of the same book in Saga District includes the story of "Setahime," suggesting they are the same deity'Saga Prefecture Place Names' Kawakami Shrine section.. There are many shrines dedicated to Yodohime (Yodohime no Kami) in northern Kyushu, centered around Saga Prefecture, with six of them, including this shrine, located along the [[Kase River]]. == Shrine Grounds == * First Torii (located outside the grounds) * Second Torii * Third Torii - '''Hizen Torii''': City-designated Important Cultural Property * West Gate - Prefecture-designated Important Cultural Property * Haiden, Chuden, Main Hall : Haiden: Five bays in front, three bays on the side, Irimoya-zukuri, Karahafu-style, with a separate Shinsenjo :Chuden: One bay in front, four bays on the side :Main Hall: Five-bay Nagare-zukuri, four bays on the side * Enshrined Shrine Yodohime Tenmangu The shrine grounds are located on the right bank of the [[Kase River]]. The West Gate, built in the 4th year of [[Genki]] (1573), is a prefecture-designated Important Cultural Property, while the third Torii, built in the 13th year of [[Keicho]] (1608), is a city-designated Important Cultural Property. The first Torii stands near Tateishi Intersection ({{Coord|33|18|28.75|N|130|15|50.15|E|region:JP-41_type:landmark|name=First Torii}}). Inside the Haiden are ceiling paintings, Thirty-Six Immortal Poets plaques, and dedication plaques. The ceiling paintings consist of 250 pieces from two scrolls: "The Tale of Yamasachihiko and Umisachihiko," relating to the deity Toyotama-hime, and the "Tale of Sugawara no Michizane," related to the enshrined deity Tenmangu. The Thirty-Six Immortal Poets plaques feature portraits of renowned poets from the Heian period with one of their representative poems. The original Thirty-Six Immortal Poets plaques, which were dedicated in the late Edo period, had deteriorated and were repainted and rededicated in 2015. Both the ceiling paintings and the Thirty-Six Immortal Poets plaques were created by the painter Yin Yusheng, who resides in Saga City and is originally from [[Dalian City]], [[China]]According to local information board. File:Yodohime-jinja honden.JPG|Main Hall File:Yodohime-jinja shaden.JPG|Haiden File:Yodohime-jinja nishimon.JPG|West Gate (Prefecture-designated Cultural Property) File:Yodohime Shrine Tenman-gu.jpg|Enshrined Shrine Yodohime Tenmangu File:Yodohime-jinja ninotorii.JPG|Second Torii File:Yodohime-jinja ichinotorii.JPG|First Torii == Annual Festivals == * Spring Festival (April 18) * Autumn Festival (October 10) * Niiname-sai (December 18) == Cultural Properties == === Nationally Designated === ==== Important Cultural Property ==== * 14 volumes of Kawakami Shrine Documents (247 items) : 10 items from the Heian period, 92 items from the Kamakura period, 85 items from the [[Nanboku-cho period]], 57 items from the Muromachi period, 3 items from the Azuchi-Momoyama period. Designated on June 6, 1980{{Cite web|Japanese book|url=https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/201/9051|title=Kawakami Shrine Documents (247 items)／Nationally Designated Cultural Property Database|accessdate=2021.08.17|publisher=Agency for Cultural Affairs}}. Deposited at the [[Saga Prefectural Library]]. :The oldest item among these is the Shazo Enjin Resolution from the 5th year of Kanji (1091){{Cite web|Japanese book|url=http://yodohime.area9.jp/category/0140122.html|title=Brief History of Hizen Ichinomiya Yodohime Shrine|accessdate=2021.08.17|publisher=Yodohime Shrine Official}}. These documents provide insights into the development of Ichinomiya in Kyushu, including relationships with the [[Dazaifu]] and the provincial office, and the trends in Kyushu during the 14th century. Senders include Seii Kokushi [[Enni]] (Saint Enni), who founded [[Tofukuji Temple]] in [[Kyoto]], and [[Imagawa Ryoshun]], the Kyushu Tandai. === Prefecture Designated === ==== Important Cultural Property ==== * West Gate - Designated on March 19, 1986{{Cite web|Japanese book|url=https://www.pref.saga.lg.jp/kiji0031451/index.html#jyu102|title=Saga Prefecture Important Cultural Property Yodohime Shrine West Gate|accessdate=2021.08.17|publisher=Saga Prefecture}}. : A [[Shikyakumon]] gate located to the northwest of the main hall, the ridge plaque copy in the Shoin documents states "Dedicated construction of the first shrine of Hizen Province Kawakami Yodohime Daimyojin West Gate by main sponsor Ryuzoji Taro Shiro Fujiwara no Ason Chikashi and Gonbu Danjo Daihitsu Takebe Nagayoshi. Constructed on an auspicious day in the third month of the fourth year of Genki (1573)". The roof is tiled, with Kirizuma-style, and the rafters are sparsely spaced. Hizen Torii.]] '''Yodohime Shrine''' (Yodohime-jinja, also known as '''Yodohime Shrine''') is a [[shrine]] located in [[Saga Prefecture]], [[Saga City]]. It is a [[Shikinai-sha]], [[Ichinomiya]] of [[Hizen Province]], and a former [[Ken-sha]] under the modern shrine ranking system. It is also written as "Yodohime Shrine" and is also known as "'''Kawakami Shrine'''" and colloquially as "Yodohime-san." == History == === Founding === According to a fragment from the '[[Hizen Province Fudoki]]' (Shinmyocho Tochu), the god Yodohime was enshrined on November 1 in the 25th year of Emperor Kinmei (564?). It is said that Ayu fish and other fish swam upstream and dived near the northern part of Setahime Shrine, suggesting it was established as a water god worship from a river-related legend recorded in the same book'Gods of Japan' Yodohime Shrine section. === Historical Overview === In the 5th year of [[Engi (era name)|Engi]] (927), the '[[Engishiki]]' [[Engishiki Jinmyocho|Jinmyocho]] lists "Yodohime Shrine" in [[Saga District]], Hizen Province, and it was included among the [[Shikinai-sha]]. In the first year of [[Kochou]] (1260), it was granted the highest rank of Shoichii (Senior First Rank). In the [[Heian period]], Tajima-no-Kami Shrine (present-day [[Tajima Shrine]]) was revered as the god of safe voyages in Hizen Province and was ranked higher than Yodohime Shrine in the 'Jinmyocho', being the only Omiya in Hizen Province. However, after the medieval period, the actual status of Yodohime Shrine, which was closer to the provincial office, rose, and it was revered as Hizen Province's Ichinomiya. In the years of [[Oho]] (1161-1163), it became the Ichinomiya of Hizen Province, and in the first year of Kochou (1261), it received the Shoichii rank. However, as mentioned later, [[Chikushi Hachiman Shrine]] also claims to be Ichinomiya. During the [[Mongol invasions of Japan]] (1281), it is said that the godly spirit of Yodohime-no-Mikoto destroyed the enemy ships. In the 7th year of [[Keicho]] (1602), Emperor Go-Yozei personally bestowed a plaque inscribed with "Great Guardian of Japan's Western Region, Hizen Province's Great Protector, Shoichii Yodohime Daimyojin Ichinomiya" (preserved in the main hall: not open to the public). This confirms that Yodohime Shrine was recognized as the Ichinomiya of Hizen Province, leading to a 60-year dispute with Chikushi Hachiman Shrine over the title. According to old records, the main hall, Heiden, and Haiden were burned down in the 10th year of Bunka (1813) and rebuilt by the Nabeshima family in the 13th year of Bunka (1816). In the 4th year of [[Meiji]] (1871), it was classified as a [[Ken-sha]] under the modern shrine ranking system. There were plans for its elevation to a Kokuheisha, but these were not realized due to the end of [[World War II]]. === Divine Rank === * Six National Histories ** [[Jogan (Japan)|Jogan]] 2nd year (860) February 8th, from Jugoi-no-ge to Jugoi-no-jo ( '[[Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku]]') - Written as "Yodohime Tenjin". ** Jogan 15th year (873) September 16th, Shogoi-no-ge ( 'Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku') - Written as "Yodohime no Kami". * Kochou first year (1260), Shoichii == Deities == * '''Yodohime-no-Mikoto''' *: Said to be the sister of [[Empress Jingu]]. Another theory states she is [[Toyotama-hime]]Deities according to the shrine's origin story.. *: In a fragment of the '[[Hizen Province Fudoki]]' (Shinmyocho Tochu), it is stated that the alternate names for "Yodohime no Kami" are "Toyohime" and "Yodohime". Another section of the same book in Saga District includes the story of "Setahime," suggesting they are the same deity'Saga Prefecture Place Names' Kawakami Shrine section.. There are many shrines dedicated to Yodohime (Yodohime no Kami) in northern Kyushu, centered around Saga Prefecture, with six of them, including this shrine, located along the [[Kase River]]. == Shrine Grounds == * First Torii (located outside the grounds) * Second Torii * Third Torii - '''Hizen Torii''': City-designated Important Cultural Property * West Gate - Prefecture-designated Important Cultural Property * Haiden, Chuden, Main Hall : Haiden: Five bays in front, three bays on the side, Irimoya-zukuri, Karahafu-style, with a separate Shinsenjo :Chuden: One bay in front, four bays on the side :Main Hall: Five-bay Nagare-zukuri, four bays on the side * Enshrined Shrine Yodohime Tenmangu The shrine grounds are located on the right bank of the [[Kase River]]. The West Gate, built in the 4th year of [[Genki]] (1573), is a prefecture-designated Important Cultural Property, while the third Torii, built in the 13th year of [[Keicho]] (1608), is a city-designated Important Cultural Property. The first Torii stands near Tateishi Intersection ({{Coord|33|18|28.75|N|130|15|50.15|E|region:JP-41_type:landmark|name=First Torii}}). Inside the Haiden are ceiling paintings, Thirty-Six Immortal Poets plaques, and dedication plaques. The ceiling paintings consist of 250 pieces from two scrolls: "The Tale of Yamasachihiko and Umisachihiko," relating to the deity Toyotama-hime, and the "Tale of Sugawara no Michizane," related to the enshrined deity Tenmangu. The Thirty-Six Immortal Poets plaques feature portraits of renowned poets from the Heian period with one of their representative poems. The original Thirty-Six Immortal Poets plaques, which were dedicated in the late Edo period, had deteriorated and were repainted and rededicated in 2015. Both the ceiling paintings and the Thirty-Six Immortal Poets plaques were created by the painter Yin Yusheng, who resides in Saga City and is originally from [[Dalian City]], [[China]]According to local information board. Designated on June 6, 1980{{Cite web|Japanese book|url=https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/201/9051|title=Kawakami Shrine Documents (247 items)／Nationally Designated Cultural Property Database|accessdate=2021.08.17|publisher=Agency for Cultural Affairs}}. These documents provide insights into the development of Ichinomiya in Kyushu, including relationships with the [[Dazaifu]] and the provincial office, and the trends in Kyushu during the 14th century. Senders include Seii Kokushi [[Enni]] (Saint Enni), who founded [[Tofukuji Temple]] in [[Kyoto]], and [[Imagawa Ryoshun]], the Kyushu Tandai. === Prefecture Designated === ==== Important Cultural Property ==== * West Gate - Designated on March 19, 1986{{Cite web|Japanese book|url=https://www.pref.saga.lg.jp/kiji0031451/index.html#jyu102|title=Saga Prefecture Important Cultural Property Yodohime Shrine West Gate|accessdate=2021.08.17|publisher=Saga Prefecture}}. : A [[Shikyakumon]] gate located to the northwest of the main hall, the ridge plaque copy in the Shoin documents states "Dedicated construction of the first shrine of Hizen Province Kawakami Yodohime Daimyojin West Gate by main sponsor Ryuzoji Taro Shiro Fujiwara no Ason Chikashi and Gonbu Danjo Daihitsu Takebe Nagayoshi. The gable has a frog decoration without carvings. The front and rear beams also have plain frog decorations, with the central bundle being rectangular. === City Designated === ==== Important Cultural Property ==== * Third Torii - Designated on October 17, 1983{{Cite web|Japanese book|url=https://www.city.saga.lg.jp/main/3887.html|title=Saga City Important Cultural Property P5|accessdate=2021.08.17|publisher=Saga City}}. : The inscription on the pillar reads "Constructed on an auspicious day in the mid-autumn of the 13th year of Keicho by Nabeshima Shinanokami Fujiwara no Ason Katsushige," indicating it was donated by Nabeshima Katsushige, the first lord of the [[Saga Domain]], in the 13th year of Keicho (1608). It is a stone Torii with a unique Hizen Torii style seen mainly in the Saga Prefecture area. Its characteristic features include three-part constructions for the Kasagi, Shimagi, Nuki, and pillars, with the Shimagi being a decorative element integrated with the Kasagi. == Others == Yodohime Shrine is designated as an Important Scenic Building in Saga City{{Cite web|Japanese book|url=https://www.city.saga.lg.jp/main/4769.html|title=Yodohime Shrine/Important Scenic Building|accessdate=2021.8.17|publisher=Saga City}}. Important Scenic Buildings in Saga City are those that have distinctive exterior features related to the region's nature, history, and culture, contributing to the formation of a favorable landscape, and are easily visible from public places such as roads{{Cite web|Japanese book|url=https://www.city.saga.lg.jp/main/333.html|title=Saga City Important Scenic Buildings|accessdate=2021.8.17|publisher=Saga City}}. == Legend == In this region, catfish are considered messengers of Yodohime-san (Yodohime-no-Mikoto) and are not eaten. There were plans for its elevation to a Kokuheisha, but these were not realized due to the end of [[World War II]]. === Divine Rank === * Six National Histories ** [[Jogan (Japan)|Jogan]] 2nd year (860) February 8th, from Jugoi-no-ge to Jugoi-no-jo ( '[[Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku]]') - Written as "Yodohime Tenjin". ** Jogan 15th year (873) September 16th, Shogoi-no-ge ( 'Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku') - Written as "Yodohime no Kami". * Kochou first year (1260), Shoichii == Deities == * '''Yodohime-no-Mikoto''' *: Said to be the sister of [[Empress Jingu]]. Another theory states she is [[Toyotama-hime]]Deities according to the shrine's origin story.. *: In a fragment of the '[[Hizen Province Fudoki]]' (Shinmyocho Tochu), it is stated that the alternate names for "Yodohime no Kami" are "Toyohime" and "Yodohime". Another section of the same book in Saga District includes the story of "Setahime," suggesting they are the same deity'Saga Prefecture Place Names' Kawakami Shrine section.. There are many shrines dedicated to Yodohime (Yodohime no Kami) in northern Kyushu, centered around Saga Prefecture, with six of them, including this shrine, located along the [[Kase River]]. == Shrine Grounds == * First Torii (located outside the grounds) * Second Torii * Third Torii - '''Hizen Torii''': City-designated Important Cultural Property * West Gate - Prefecture-designated Important Cultural Property * Haiden, Chuden, Main Hall : Haiden: Five bays in front, three bays on the side, Irimoya-zukuri, Karahafu-style, with a separate Shinsenjo :Chuden: One bay in front, four bays on the side :Main Hall: Five-bay Nagare-zukuri, four bays on the side * Enshrined Shrine Yodohime Tenmangu The shrine grounds are located on the right bank of the [[Kase River]]. The West Gate, built in the 4th year of [[Genki]] (1573), is a prefecture-designated Important Cultural Property, while the third Torii, built in the 13th year of [[Keicho]] (1608), is a city-designated Important Cultural Property. The first Torii stands near Tateishi Intersection ({{Coord|33|18|28.75|N|130|15|50.15|E|region:JP-41_type:landmark|name=First Torii}}). Inside the Haiden are ceiling paintings, Thirty-Six Immortal Poets plaques, and dedication plaques. The ceiling paintings consist of 250 pieces from two scrolls: "The Tale of Yamasachihiko and Umisachihiko," relating to the deity Toyotama-hime, and the "Tale of Sugawara no Michizane," related to the enshrined deity Tenmangu. The Thirty-Six Immortal Poets plaques feature portraits of renowned poets from the Heian period with one of their representative poems. The original Thirty-Six Immortal Poets plaques, which were dedicated in the late Edo period, had deteriorated and were repainted and rededicated in 2015. Both the ceiling paintings and the Thirty-Six Immortal Poets plaques were created by the painter Yin Yusheng, who resides in Saga City and is originally from [[Dalian City]], [[China]]According to local information board. File:Yodohime-jinja honden.JPG|Main Hall File:Yodohime-jinja shaden.JPG|Haiden File:Yodohime-jinja nishimon.JPG|West Gate (Prefecture-designated Cultural Property) File:Yodohime Shrine Tenman-gu.jpg|Enshrined Shrine Yodohime Tenmangu File:Yodohime-jinja ninotorii.JPG|Second Torii File:Yodohime-jinja ichinotorii.JPG|First Torii == Annual Festivals == * Spring Festival (April 18) * Autumn Festival (October 10) * Niiname-sai (December 18) == Cultural Properties == === Nationally Designated === ==== Important Cultural Property ==== * 14 volumes of Kawakami Shrine Documents (247 items) : 10 items from the Heian period, 92 items from the Kamakura period, 85 items from the [[Nanboku-cho period]], 57 items from the Muromachi period, 3 items from the Azuchi-Momoyama period. Designated on June 6, 1980{{Cite web|Japanese book|url=https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/201/9051|title=Kawakami Shrine Documents (247 items)／Nationally Designated Cultural Property Database|accessdate=2021.08.17|publisher=Agency for Cultural Affairs}}. Deposited at the [[Saga Prefectural Library]]. :The oldest item among these is the Shazo Enjin Resolution from the 5th year of Kanji (1091){{Cite web|Japanese book|url=http://yodohime.area9.jp/category/0140122.html|title=Brief History of Hizen Ichinomiya Yodohime Shrine|accessdate=2021.08.17|publisher=Yodohime Shrine Official}}. These documents provide insights into the development of Ichinomiya in Kyushu, including relationships with the [[Dazaifu]] and the provincial office, and the trends in Kyushu during the 14th century. Senders include Seii Kokushi [[Enni]] (Saint Enni), who founded [[Tofukuji Temple]] in [[Kyoto]], and [[Imagawa Ryoshun]], the Kyushu Tandai. === Prefecture Designated === ==== Important Cultural Property ==== * West Gate - Designated on March 19, 1986{{Cite web|Japanese book|url=https://www.pref.saga.lg.jp/kiji0031451/index.html#jyu102|title=Saga Prefecture Important Cultural Property Yodohime Shrine West Gate|accessdate=2021.08.17|publisher=Saga Prefecture}}. : A [[Shikyakumon]] gate located to the northwest of the main hall, the ridge plaque copy in the Shoin documents states "Dedicated construction of the first shrine of Hizen Province Kawakami Yodohime Daimyojin West Gate by main sponsor Ryuzoji Taro Shiro Fujiwara no Ason Chikashi and Gonbu Danjo Daihitsu Takebe Nagayoshi. Constructed on an auspicious day in the third month of the fourth year of Genki (1573)". The roof is tiled, with Kirizuma-style, and the rafters are sparsely spaced. The gable has a frog decoration without carvings. The front and rear beams also have plain frog decorations, with the central bundle being rectangular. === City Designated === ==== Important Cultural Property ==== * Third Torii - Designated on October 17, 1983{{Cite web|Japanese book|url=https://www.city.saga.lg.jp/main/3887.html|title=Saga City Important Cultural Property P5|accessdate=2021.08.17|publisher=Saga City}}. : The inscription on the pillar reads "Constructed on an auspicious day in the mid-autumn of the 13th year of Keicho by Nabeshima Shinanokami Fujiwara no Ason Katsushige," indicating it was donated by Nabeshima Katsushige, the first lord of the [[Saga Domain]], in the 13th year of Keicho (1608). It is a stone Torii with a unique Hizen Torii style seen mainly in the Saga Prefecture area. Its characteristic features include three-part constructions for the Kasagi, Shimagi, Nuki, and pillars, with the Shimagi being a decorative element integrated with the Kasagi. == Others == Yodohime Shrine is designated as an Important Scenic Building in Saga City{{Cite web|Japanese book|url=https://www.city.saga.lg.jp/main/4769.html|title=Yodohime Shrine/Important Scenic Building|accessdate=2021.8.17|publisher=Saga City}}. Important Scenic Buildings in Saga City are those that have distinctive exterior features related to the region's nature, history, and culture, contributing to the formation of a favorable landscape, and are easily visible from public places such as roads{{Cite web|Japanese book|url=https://www.city.saga.lg.jp/main/333.html|title=Saga City Important Scenic Buildings|accessdate=2021.8.17|publisher=Saga City}}. == Legend == In this region, catfish are considered messengers of Yodohime-san (Yodohime-no-Mikoto) and are not eaten. The Hizen Fudoki's section on the god of Kawakami states, "Some people who fear the fish do not suffer, while others who catch and eat it die," and it is believed that this fish corresponds to the catfish in this area. == Front Gate Sweets == * Shiratama Manju - Originates from a legend related to the shrine. == Local Information == '''Location''' * [[Saga Prefecture]][[Saga City]] Yamatomachi Kawakami 1 '''Access''' * From [[JR Kyushu]] [[Nagasaki Main Line]] [[Saga Station]] ** Bus: [[Showa Bus]] to "Kawakami Bridge" bus stop (immediate walk after getting off) ** Car: About 20 minutes * Previously, there was a Hizen Kawakami Station, the terminus of the [[Saga Electric Railway]], across the Kase River. 旧[[県社]] |創建 = [[欽明天皇]]25年（[[564年]]?） |本殿 = 五間社[[流造]] |別名 = 河上神社、淀姫さん |札所等 = |例祭 = [[4月18日]]、[[12月18日]] |神事 = 秋祭（おくんち、[[10月10日]]） |地図 = {{Location map|Japan Saga|label=與止日女神社|position=bottom|width=200|float=center|caption=|mark=Shinto torii icon vermillion.svg|marksize=20}}{{maplink2|frame=yes|plain=yes|type=point|zoom=12|frame-align=center|frame-width=200}} }} {{座標一覧}} [[File:Yodohime-jinja keidai.JPG|thumb|200px|right|境内と[[嘉瀬川]]]] [[File:Yodohime-jinja sannnotorii.JPG|thumb|200px|right|三の鳥居（市指定文化財）
肥前鳥居。]] '''與止日女神社'''（よどひめじんじゃ、'''与止日女神社'''）は、[[佐賀県]][[佐賀市]]にある[[神社]]。[[式内社]]、[[肥前国]][[一宮]]で、[[近代社格制度|旧社格]]は[[県社]]。 「淀姫神社」とも表記され、別称として「'''河上神社'''」、通称として「淀姫さん」とも呼ばれている。 == 歴史 == === 創建 === 『[[肥前国風土記]]』逸文（神名帳頭注）によれば、[[欽明天皇]]25年（[[564年]]?）11月1日に與止姫の神が鎮座したという。 世田姫神社の北に川上があり鮎や謂魚が逆流して潜ったりしていたとあり、同書に収録された川にまつわる説話から、[[水神]]信仰として成立したものと見られている『日本の神々』与止日女神社項。 === 概史 === [[延長 (元号)|延長]]5年（[[927年]]）の『[[延喜式]]』[[延喜式神名帳|神名帳]]では[[肥前国]][[佐嘉郡]]に「與止日女神社」と記載され、[[式内社]]に列した。[[弘長]]元年（[[1260年]]）に最高位の正一位の[[神階]]を授けられた。 [[平安時代]]には、肥前国では田島坐神社（現 [[田島神社]]）が安全航海の神として崇敬され、神階も当社より上で『神名帳』では肥前国唯一の大社に列していた。しかしながら、中世以降は[[国衙]]に近い当社の実質的地位が高まり、肥前国一宮として崇敬されたという。[[応保]]年間（1161年-1163年）には肥前国一の宮になり、弘長元年（1261年）正一位を受けた。ただし、後述のように[[千栗八幡宮]]も一宮を称している。 [[弘安の役]]（[[1281年]]）では與止日女大神の[[霊魂#日本|神霊]]が敵の船を摧いたと伝えられる。 [[慶長]]7年（[[1602年]]）に[[後陽成天皇]]が自ら「大日本国鎮西肥前州大一之鎮守　宗廟河上山正一位淀姫大明神一宮」と宸筆した[[勅額]]を賜る（本殿に現存：非公開）。すなわち当社が肥前国一宮であるとするものであるが、千栗八幡宮も肥前国一宮とされていたことから、両社の間で60年にわたる紛争が起こった。 古記録によると、本殿、幣殿、拝殿は、文化10年（1813年）に焼失し、文化13年（1816年）に鍋島家により再建された。 [[明治]]4年（[[1871年]]）には[[近代社格制度]]において[[県社]]に列した。国幣社への昇格も進められていたが、[[第二次世界大戦]]の終結により実現しなかった。 === 神階 === * 六国史 ** [[貞観 (日本)|貞観]]2年（[[860年]]）2月8日、従五位下から従五位上 （『[[日本三代実録]]』） - 表記は「予等比咩天神」。 ** 貞観15年（[[873年]]）9月16日、正五位下 （『日本三代実録』） - 表記は「予等比咩神」。 * [[弘長]]元年（[[1260年]]）、正一位 == 祭神 == ; 與止日女命 （よどひめのみこと） : [[神功皇后]]の妹という。また一説に、[[豊玉姫]]であるとも伝える祭神は神社由緒書による。。 : 『[[肥前国風土記]]』逸文（神名帳頭注）には、「與止姫神」のまたの名を「豊姫」「淀姫」というとある。また、同書佐嘉郡条には「世田姫」の説話が載り、同一神と見られている『佐賀県の地名』河上神社項。。 佐賀県を中心とする北九州地方には、與止日女神（淀姫神）を祀る神社が多数あり、そのうち当社を含めた6社が[[嘉瀬川]]流域にある。 == 境内社 == * 與止日女天満宮：[[菅原道真]]公を祀る。 == 境内 == * 一ノ鳥居（境外に建つ） * 二ノ鳥居 * 三ノ鳥居 - '''肥前鳥居'''：市指定重要文化財 * 西門 - 県指定重要文化財 * 拝殿・中殿・本殿 : 拝殿：正面五間、側面三間、入母屋造、唐破風付、別棟神饌所付 :中殿：正面一間、側面四間 :本殿：五間社流造、側面四間 * 境内社 與止日女天満宮 境内は[[嘉瀬川]]そばの右岸に位置する。西門は[[元亀]]4年（[[1573年]]）造営で県の重要文化財に、三の鳥居は[[慶長]]13年（[[1608年]]）造営の肥前鳥居で市の重要文化財に指定されている。一の鳥居は立石交差点付近に立つ（{{Coord|33|18|28.75|N|130|15|50.15|E|region:JP-41_type:landmark|name=一の鳥居}}）。 拝殿内に天井絵馬、三十六歌仙絵札額、奉納額などがある。天井絵馬は、祭神の與止日女命は一節によると豊玉姫ともいわれ、豊玉姫と関係ある「[[山幸彦と海幸彦|山幸彦海幸彦]]縁起絵巻」と境内社の天満社にちなむ「[[菅原道真|菅原道真公]]絵巻」の2巻から構成された250枚からなっている。三十六歌仙絵札額は、平安時代の和歌の名人[[三十六歌仙]]の人物画に代表的な和歌1首ずつを書き込んだ絵札である。元々、江戸時代後期に奉納されていた三十六歌仙絵札が老朽化していたため、新たに描きなおし2015年（平成27年）に奉納されたもの。天井絵馬、三十六歌仙絵札額は、ともに佐賀市在住・[[中国]][[大連市|大連]]出身の[[画家]]、尹雨生の作である現地案内板による。 ファイル:Yodohime-jinja honden.JPG|本殿 ファイル:Yodohime-jinja shaden.JPG|拝殿 ファイル:Yodohime-jinja nishimon.JPG|西門（県指定文化財） ファイル:Yodohime Shrine Tenman-gu.jpg|境内社 與止日女天満宮 ファイル:Yodohime-jinja ninotorii.JPG|二の鳥居 ファイル:Yodohime-jinja ichinotorii.JPG|一の鳥居 == 祭事 == * 春祭 （4月18日） * 秋祭 （10月10日） * 新嘗祭 （12月18日） == 文化財 == === 国指定 === ==== 重要文化財 ==== * 河上神社文書14巻（247通） : 平安時代10通、鎌倉時代92通、[[南北朝時代 (日本)|南北朝時代]]85通、室町時代57通、安土桃山時代3通。1980年（昭和55年）6月6日指定{{Cite web|和書|url=https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/201/9051|title=河上神社文書（二百四十七通）／国指定文化財等データーベース|accessdate=2021.08.17|publisher=文化庁}}。[[佐賀県立図書館]]に寄託。 :この中で最も古いものは寛治5年（1091年）の社増円尋解状である{{Cite web|和書|url=http://yodohime.area9.jp/category/0140122.html|title=肥前一之宮 與止日女神社略記|accessdate=2021.08.17|publisher=與止日女神社公式}}。これら文章は、九州における一宮の発展を伝えたもので、[[大宰府]]・[[国衙]]（こくが）関係文書は、当社と大宰府・国衙の関係を示し、南北朝関係文書は、十四世紀の九州の動向が示されている。差出人に、[[京都]]・[[東福寺]]を開山した[[円爾|聖一国師]]（[[円爾]]）、[[九州探題]]の[[今川貞世|今川了俊]]などがある。 === 県指定 === ==== 重要文化財 ==== * 西門 - 1986年（昭和61年）3月19日指定{{Cite web|和書|url=https://www.pref.saga.lg.jp/kiji0031451/index.html#jyu102|title=佐賀県重要文化財　与止日女神社西門|accessdate=2021.08.17|publisher=佐賀県}}。 : 本殿西北方に建つ[[四脚門]]で、相院文書中にある[[棟札]]の[[写し]]に「奉造立肥前国第一宮河上淀姫大明神西ノ門一宇大檀那龍造寺太郎四郎藤原鎮賢神代刑部大輔武邊長良願主蓮乗院増純　元亀四歳癸酉三月吉祥日」とあり元亀4年（1573）年の建立である。屋根は本瓦葺き、切妻造り、垂木は一幹、疎垂木である。破風は、ひれ付き、拝懸魚、降懸魚、これらに木製菊形の6葉が飾られている。妻は虹梁蟇股式で蟇股は彫刻のない板蟇股である。正面、背面の梁上の中備えにも板蟇股を配し、中央の真束は角形である。 === 市指定 === ==== 重要文化財 ==== * 三の鳥居 - 1983年（昭和58年）10月17日指定{{Cite web|和書|url=https://www.city.saga.lg.jp/main/3887.html|title=佐賀市重要文化財P5|accessdate=2021.08.17|publisher=佐賀市}}。 : 柱の銘文に、「慶長十三歳仲秋吉祥日　鍋島信濃守藤原朝臣勝茂」とあり、[[佐賀藩|鍋島]]初代藩主[[鍋島勝茂]]が[[慶長]]13年([[1608年|1608]]年)に寄進したものである。石造の鳥居で、主に佐賀県周辺地域で見られる独特の形式の肥前鳥居である。特徴としては、笠木・島木・貫・柱が三本継ぎとなっていて、島木は形骸化し笠木と一体化し両端が流線形になっている。 == その他 == 佐賀市景観重要建造物等に指定されている{{Cite web|和書|url=https://www.city.saga.lg.jp/main/4769.html|title=與止日女神社／景観重要建造物|accessdate=2021.8.17|publisher=佐賀市}}。 佐賀市景観重要建造物等は、「地域の自然、歴史、文化等からみて、建造物の外観が景観上の特徴を持ち、良好な景観形成に重要なもので、道路など公共の場所から容易に見ることができるもの」を対象とされている{{Cite web|和書|url=https://www.city.saga.lg.jp/main/333.html|title=佐賀市景観重要建造物等|accessdate=2021.8.17|publisher=佐賀市}}。 == 伝説 == この地域では、なまずは、淀姫さん（與止日女命のこと）のお使いとされ、食すことがない。 肥前風土記の川上の神の条に「或は人其の魚を畏むものは殃無く、或は人捕り食へば死ぬこと有り」とあり、その魚は当地において、[[なまず]]に相当すると考えられている。 == 門前菓子 == *白玉饅頭 - 神社に伝わる伝説に由来する。 == 現地情報 == '''所在地''' * [[佐賀県]][[佐賀市]]大和町大字川上1 '''交通アクセス''' * [[九州旅客鉄道]]（JR九州）[[長崎本線]] [[佐賀駅]]から ** バス：[[昭和自動車|昭和バス]]で「川上橋」バス停下車 （下車後徒歩すぐ） ** 車：約20分 * かつては[[嘉瀬川]]を挟んで[[佐賀電気軌道]]の終点である肥前川上駅が存在した。 '''周辺''' * [[肥前国庁跡]] * [[船塚古墳 (佐賀市)|船塚古墳]] - 佐賀県最大の前方後円墳。 == 脚注 == {{脚注ヘルプ}} {{reflist}} == 参考文献 == * 神社由緒書 * 『日本歴史地名体系 佐賀県の地名』（[[平凡社]]）佐賀郡 河上神社項 * [[杉谷昭]]「与止日女神社」（[[谷川健一]] 編『日本の神々 -神社と聖地- 1 九州』（[[白水社]]）） == 関連項目 == * [[千栗八幡宮]] - 肥前国一宮を称するもう1つの神社。 * [[與杼神社]] * [[月日神社]] - 與止日女命を祀る[[奈良市]]の神社。 * [[與賀神社]] - 與止日女命を祀る == 外部リンク == {{Commonscat|Yodohime-jinja}} * [https://yodohime-jinja.jimdo.com/?logout=1/ 與止日女神社]（公式サイト） * [http://www.sagabai.com/main/?cont=kanko&fid=57 與止日女神社]（[[佐賀市観光協会]]） {{神道 横}} {{DEFAULTSORT:よとひめしんしや}} [[Category:佐賀県の神社]] [[Category:佐賀市の建築物]] [[Category:佐賀市の歴史]] [[Category:肥前国の式内社]] [[Category:一宮]] [[Category:佐賀県の旧県社]] [[Category:佐賀県の重要文化財]] [[Category:肥前国|社1]] [[Category:佐賀県指定有形文化財]] [[Category:佐賀県内の市町村指定有形文化財]]

Shrine grounds |Location = [[Saga Prefecture]][[Saga City]] Yamatomachi Kawakami 1 |Position = {{WikiCoordinates2degrees|33|19|34.7|N|130|16|6|E|display=inline,title}} |Deity = Yodohime-no-Mikoto |Sacred Object = |Rank = [[Shikinai-sha]] (small)
[[Hizen Province]] [[Ichinomiya]]
Former [[Ken-sha]] |Founding = 25th year of Emperor Kinmei (564?) |Main Hall = Five-bay Nagare-zukuri |Alias = Kawakami Shrine, Yodohime-san |Pilgrimage = |Annual Festival = [[April 18]], [[December 18]] |Rituals = Autumn Festival (Okunchi, [[October 10]]) |Map = {{Location map|Japan Saga|label=Yodohime Shrine|position=bottom|width=200|float=center|caption=|mark=Shinto torii icon vermillion.svg|marksize=20}}{{maplink2|frame=yes|plain=yes|type=point|zoom=12|frame-align=center|frame-width=200}} }} {{Coordinates list}} [[File:Yodohime-jinja keidai.JPG|thumb|200px|right|Shrine grounds and [[Kase River]]]] [[File:Yodohime-jinja sannnotorii.JPG|thumb|200px|right|Third Torii (City-designated cultural property)
Hizen Torii.]] '''Yodohime Shrine''' (Yodohime-jinja, also known as '''Yodohime Shrine''') is a [[shrine]] located in [[Saga Prefecture]], [[Saga City]]. It is a [[Shikinai-sha]], [[Ichinomiya]] of [[Hizen Province]], and a former [[Ken-sha]] under the modern shrine ranking system. It is also written as "Yodohime Shrine" and is also known as "'''Kawakami Shrine'''" and colloquially as "Yodohime-san." == History == === Founding === According to a fragment from the '[[Hizen Province Fudoki]]' (Shinmyocho Tochu), the god Yodohime was enshrined on November 1 in the 25th year of Emperor Kinmei (564?). It is said that Ayu fish and other fish swam upstream and dived near the northern part of Setahime Shrine, suggesting it was established as a water god worship from a river-related legend recorded in the same book'Gods of Japan' Yodohime Shrine section. === Historical Overview === In the 5th year of [[Engi (era name)|Engi]] (927), the '[[Engishiki]]' [[Engishiki Jinmyocho|Jinmyocho]] lists "Yodohime Shrine" in [[Saga District]], Hizen Province, and it was included among the [[Shikinai-sha]]. In the first year of [[Kochou]] (1260), it was granted the highest rank of Shoichii (Senior First Rank). In the [[Heian period]], Tajima-no-Kami Shrine (present-day [[Tajima Shrine]]) was revered as the god of safe voyages in Hizen Province and was ranked higher than Yodohime Shrine in the 'Jinmyocho', being the only Omiya in Hizen Province. However, after the medieval period, the actual status of Yodohime Shrine, which was closer to the provincial office, rose, and it was revered as Hizen Province's Ichinomiya. In the years of [[Oho]] (1161-1163), it became the Ichinomiya of Hizen Province, and in the first year of Kochou (1261), it received the Shoichii rank. However, as mentioned later, [[Chikushi Hachiman Shrine]] also claims to be Ichinomiya. During the [[Mongol invasions of Japan]] (1281), it is said that the godly spirit of Yodohime-no-Mikoto destroyed the enemy ships. In the 7th year of [[Keicho]] (1602), Emperor Go-Yozei personally bestowed a plaque inscribed with "Great Guardian of Japan's Western Region, Hizen Province's Great Protector, Shoichii Yodohime Daimyojin Ichinomiya" (preserved in the main hall: not open to the public). This confirms that Yodohime Shrine was recognized as the Ichinomiya of Hizen Province, leading to a 60-year dispute with Chikushi Hachiman Shrine over the title. According to old records, the main hall, Heiden, and Haiden were burned down in the 10th year of Bunka (1813) and rebuilt by the Nabeshima family in the 13th year of Bunka (1816). In the 4th year of [[Meiji]] (1871), it was classified as a [[Ken-sha]] under the modern shrine ranking system. There were plans for its elevation to a Kokuheisha, but these were not realized due to the end of [[World War II]]. === Divine Rank === * Six National Histories ** [[Jogan (Japan)|Jogan]] 2nd year (860) February 8th, from Jugoi-no-ge to Jugoi-no-jo ( '[[Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku]]') - Written as "Yodohime Tenjin". ** Jogan 15th year (873) September 16th, Shogoi-no-ge ( 'Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku') - Written as "Yodohime no Kami". * Kochou first year (1260), Shoichii == Deities == * '''Yodohime-no-Mikoto''' *: Said to be the sister of [[Empress Jingu]]. Another theory states she is [[Toyotama-hime]]Deities according to the shrine's origin story.. *: In a fragment of the '[[Hizen Province Fudoki]]' (Shinmyocho Tochu), it is stated that the alternate names for "Yodohime no Kami" are "Toyohime" and "Yodohime". Another section of the same book in Saga District includes the story of "Setahime," suggesting they are the same deity'Saga Prefecture Place Names' Kawakami Shrine section.. There are many shrines dedicated to Yodohime (Yodohime no Kami) in northern Kyushu, centered around Saga Prefecture, with six of them, including this shrine, located along the [[Kase River]]. == Shrine Grounds == * First Torii (located outside the grounds) * Second Torii * Third Torii - '''Hizen Torii''': City-designated Important Cultural Property * West Gate - Prefecture-designated Important Cultural Property * Haiden, Chuden, Main Hall : Haiden: Five bays in front, three bays on the side, Irimoya-zukuri, Karahafu-style, with a separate Shinsenjo :Chuden: One bay in front, four bays on the side :Main Hall: Five-bay Nagare-zukuri, four bays on the side * Enshrined Shrine Yodohime Tenmangu The shrine grounds are located on the right bank of the [[Kase River]]. The West Gate, built in the 4th year of [[Genki]] (1573), is a prefecture-designated Important Cultural Property, while the third Torii, built in the 13th year of [[Keicho]] (1608), is a city-designated Important Cultural Property. The first Torii stands near Tateishi Intersection ({{Coord|33|18|28.75|N|130|15|50.15|E|region:JP-41_type:landmark|name=First Torii}}). Inside the Haiden are ceiling paintings, Thirty-Six Immortal Poets plaques, and dedication plaques. The ceiling paintings consist of 250 pieces from two scrolls: "The Tale of Yamasachihiko and Umisachihiko," relating to the deity Toyotama-hime, and the "Tale of Sugawara no Michizane," related to the enshrined deity Tenmangu. The Thirty-Six Immortal Poets plaques feature portraits of renowned poets from the Heian period with one of their representative poems. The original Thirty-Six Immortal Poets plaques, which were dedicated in the late Edo period, had deteriorated and were repainted and rededicated in 2015. Both the ceiling paintings and the Thirty-Six Immortal Poets plaques were created by the painter Yin Yusheng, who resides in Saga City and is originally from [[Dalian City]], [[China]]According to local information board. File:Yodohime-jinja honden.JPG|Main Hall File:Yodohime-jinja shaden.JPG|Haiden File:Yodohime-jinja nishimon.JPG|West Gate (Prefecture-designated Cultural Property) File:Yodohime Shrine Tenman-gu.jpg|Enshrined Shrine Yodohime Tenmangu File:Yodohime-jinja ninotorii.JPG|Second Torii File:Yodohime-jinja ichinotorii.JPG|First Torii == Annual Festivals == * Spring Festival (April 18) * Autumn Festival (October 10) * Niiname-sai (December 18) == Cultural Properties == === Nationally Designated === ==== Important Cultural Property ==== * 14 volumes of Kawakami Shrine Documents (247 items) : 10 items from the Heian period, 92 items from the Kamakura period, 85 items from the [[Nanboku-cho period]], 57 items from the Muromachi period, 3 items from the Azuchi-Momoyama period. Designated on June 6, 1980{{Cite web|Japanese book|url=https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/201/9051|title=Kawakami Shrine Documents (247 items)／Nationally Designated Cultural Property Database|accessdate=2021.08.17|publisher=Agency for Cultural Affairs}}. Deposited at the [[Saga Prefectural Library]]. :The oldest item among these is the Shazo Enjin Resolution from the 5th year of Kanji (1091){{Cite web|Japanese book|url=http://yodohime.area9.jp/category/0140122.html|title=Brief History of Hizen Ichinomiya Yodohime Shrine|accessdate=2021.08.17|publisher=Yodohime Shrine Official}}. These documents provide insights into the development of Ichinomiya in Kyushu, including relationships with the [[Dazaifu]] and the provincial office, and the trends in Kyushu during the 14th century. Senders include Seii Kokushi [[Enni]] (Saint Enni), who founded [[Tofukuji Temple]] in [[Kyoto]], and [[Imagawa Ryoshun]], the Kyushu Tandai. === Prefecture Designated === ==== Important Cultural Property ==== * West Gate - Designated on March 19, 1986{{Cite web|Japanese book|url=https://www.pref.saga.lg.jp/kiji0031451/index.html#jyu102|title=Saga Prefecture Important Cultural Property Yodohime Shrine West Gate|accessdate=2021.08.17|publisher=Saga Prefecture}}. : A [[Shikyakumon]] gate located to the northwest of the main hall, the ridge plaque copy in the Shoin documents states "Dedicated construction of the first shrine of Hizen Province Kawakami Yodohime Daimyojin West Gate by main sponsor Ryuzoji Taro Shiro Fujiwara no Ason Chikashi and Gonbu Danjo Daihitsu Takebe Nagayoshi. Constructed on an auspicious day in the third month of the fourth year of Genki (1573)". The roof is tiled, with Kirizuma-style, and the rafters are sparsely spaced. The gable has a frog decoration without carvings. The front and rear beams also have plain frog decorations, with the central bundle being rectangular. === City Designated === ==== Important Cultural Property ==== * Third Torii - Designated on October 17, 1983{{Cite web|Japanese book|url=https://www.city.saga.lg.jp/main/3887.html|title=Saga City Important Cultural Property P5|accessdate=2021.08.17|publisher=Saga City}}. : The inscription on the pillar reads "Constructed on an auspicious day in the mid-autumn of the 13th year of Keicho by Nabeshima Shinanokami Fujiwara no Ason Katsushige," indicating it was donated by Nabeshima Katsushige, the first lord of the [[Saga Domain]], in the 13th year of Keicho (1608). It is a stone Torii with a unique Hizen Torii style seen mainly in the Saga Prefecture area. Its characteristic features include three-part constructions for the Kasagi, Shimagi, Nuki, and pillars, with the Shimagi being a decorative element integrated with the Kasagi. == Others == Yodohime Shrine is designated as an Important Scenic Building in Saga City{{Cite web|Japanese book|url=https://www.city.saga.lg.jp/main/4769.html|title=Yodohime Shrine/Important Scenic Building|accessdate=2021.8.17|publisher=Saga City}}. Important Scenic Buildings in Saga City are those that have distinctive exterior features related to the region's nature, history, and culture, contributing to the formation of a favorable landscape, and are easily visible from public places such as roads{{Cite web|Japanese book|url=https://www.city.saga.lg.jp/main/333.html|title=Saga City Important Scenic Buildings|accessdate=2021.8.17|publisher=Saga City}}. == Legend == In this region, catfish are considered messengers of Yodohime-san (Yodohime-no-Mikoto) and are not eaten. The Hizen Fudoki's section on the god of Kawakami states, "Some people who fear the fish do not suffer, while others who catch and eat it die," and it is believed that this fish corresponds to the catfish in this area. == Front Gate Sweets == * Shiratama Manju - Originates from a legend related to the shrine. == Local Information == '''Location''' * [[Saga Prefecture]][[Saga City]] Yamatomachi Kawakami 1 '''Access''' * From [[JR Kyushu]] [[Nagasaki Main Line]] [[Saga Station]] ** Bus: [[Showa Bus]] to "Kawakami Bridge" bus stop (immediate walk after getting off) ** Car: About 20 minutes * Previously, there was a Hizen Kawakami Station, the terminus of the [[Saga Electric Railway]], across the Kase River. '''Nearby''' * [[Hizen Provincial Government Ruins]] * [[Funatsuka Burial Mound (Saga City)|Funatsuka Burial Mound]] - The largest keyhole-shaped burial mound in Saga Prefecture. == References == {{Reflist}} == Bibliography == * Shrine origin story * 'Japanese Historical Place Names Saga Prefecture Place Names' (Heibonsha) Saga District Kawakami Shrine section * [[Akira Sugitani]] 'Yodohime Shrine' (Edited by [[Kenichi Tanigawa]] 'Japanese Gods - Shrines and Sacred Sites - 1 Kyushu' (Hakusuisha)) == See also == * [[Chikushi Hachiman Shrine]] - Another shrine claiming to be Ichinomiya of Hizen Province. * [[Yodo Shrine]] * [[Tsukihi Shrine]] - A shrine in [[Nara City]] enshrining Yodohime-no-Mikoto. * [[Yoka Shrine]] - Enshrining Yodohime-no-Mikoto == External Links == {{Commonscat|Yodohime-jinja}} * [https://yodohime-jinja.jimdo.com/?logout=1/ Yodohime Shrine] (official site) * [http://www.sagabai.com/main/?cont=kanko&fid=57 Yodohime Shrine] (Saga City Tourism Association) {{Shinto Side}} {{DEFAULTSORT:Yodohime Shrine}} [[Category:Shrines in Saga Prefecture]] [[Category:Buildings and structures in Saga City]] [[Category:History of Saga City]] [[Category:Shikinai-sha of Hizen Province]] [[Category:Ichinomiya]] [[Category:Ken-sha]] [[Category:Important Cultural Properties of Saga Prefecture]] [[Category:Hizen Province|Shrine1]] [[Category:Prefecture-designated Tangible Cultural Properties in Saga Prefecture]] [[Category:Municipal-designated Tangible Cultural Properties in Saga Prefecture]] ==History== ''Yodohime jinja'' was founded in the sixth century. It enshrines the ''[[kami]]'' of the grandmother of [[Emperor Jimmu]]. It was one of two chief [[Shinto shrine]] (''[[ichinomiya]]'') of [[Hizen Province]] and Saga Prefecture.Picken, Stuart. (2004). [https://books.google.com/books?id=v7Xs1NzMMHMC&pg=PA377 ''Sourcebook in Shinto: Selected Documents,'' p. 377]; [http://eos.kokugakuin.ac.jp/modules/xwords/images/uploads/EOS070712Ab.pdf "Nationwide List of ''Ichinomiya''," p. 3] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130517061440/http://eos.kokugakuin.ac.jp/modules/xwords/images/uploads/EOS070712Ab.pdf |date=2013-05-17 }}; retrieved 2012-8-23. ==References== {{Reflist}} ==Other websites== {{Commons category-inline|Yodohime-jinja}} * [http://yodohime.area9.jp/ Yodohime jinja website {{in lang|ja}}] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121114185918/http://yodohime.area9.jp/ |date=2012-11-14 }} {{coord|33|32|N|130|26|E|scale:500000|display=title}} {{Japan-stub}} {{DEFAULTSORT:Yodohime jinja}} [[Category:Shinto shrines in Saga Prefecture]] [[Category:6th-century establishments in Asia]] [[Category:Ichinomiya]] [[Category:Fuken-sha]] [[Category:Uncategorized_Shinto_shrines]][[en:Yodohime Shrine]][[Category:Uncategorized_Shinto_shrines]] [[Category:[[Category:Original pages]] [[Category:Ff]][[ja:與止日女神社]] [[simple:Yodohime Shrine]] [[en:Yodohime Shrine]] ]]

There were plans for its elevation to a Kokuheisha, but these were not realized due to the end of [[World War II]]. === Divine Rank === * Six National Histories ** [[Jogan (Japan)|Jogan]] 2nd year (860) February 8th, from Jugoi-no-ge to Jugoi-no-jo ( '[[Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku]]') - Written as "Yodohime Tenjin". ** Jogan 15th year (873) September 16th, Shogoi-no-ge ( 'Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku') - Written as "Yodohime no Kami". * Kochou first year (1260), Shoichii == Deities == * '''Yodohime-no-Mikoto''' *: Said to be the sister of [[Empress Jingu]]. Another theory states she is [[Toyotama-hime]]Deities according to the shrine's origin story.. *: In a fragment of the '[[Hizen Province Fudoki]]' (Shinmyocho Tochu), it is stated that the alternate names for "Yodohime no Kami" are "Toyohime" and "Yodohime". Another section of the same book in Saga District includes the story of "Setahime," suggesting they are the same deity'Saga Prefecture Place Names' Kawakami Shrine section.. There are many shrines dedicated to Yodohime (Yodohime no Kami) in northern Kyushu, centered around Saga Prefecture, with six of them, including this shrine, located along the [[Kase River]]. == Shrine Grounds == * First Torii (located outside the grounds) * Second Torii * Third Torii - '''Hizen Torii''': City-designated Important Cultural Property * West Gate - Prefecture-designated Important Cultural Property * Haiden, Chuden, Main Hall : Haiden: Five bays in front, three bays on the side, Irimoya-zukuri, Karahafu-style, with a separate Shinsenjo :Chuden: One bay in front, four bays on the side :Main Hall: Five-bay Nagare-zukuri, four bays on the side * Enshrined Shrine Yodohime Tenmangu The shrine grounds are located on the right bank of the [[Kase River]]. The West Gate, built in the 4th year of [[Genki]] (1573), is a prefecture-designated Important Cultural Property, while the third Torii, built in the 13th year of [[Keicho]] (1608), is a city-designated Important Cultural Property. The ceiling paintings consist of 250 pieces from two scrolls: "The Tale of Yamasachihiko and Umisachihiko," relating to the deity Toyotama-hime, and the "Tale of Sugawara no Michizane," related to the enshrined deity Tenmangu. The Thirty-Six Immortal Poets plaques feature portraits of renowned poets from the Heian period with one of their representative poems. The original Thirty-Six Immortal Poets plaques, which were dedicated in the late Edo period, had deteriorated and were repainted and rededicated in 2015. Deposited at the [[Saga Prefectural Library]]. :The oldest item among these is the Shazo Enjin Resolution from the 5th year of Kanji (1091){{Cite web|Japanese book|url=http://yodohime.area9.jp/category/0140122.html|title=Brief History of Hizen Ichinomiya Yodohime Shrine|accessdate=2021.08.17|publisher=Yodohime Shrine Official}}. These documents provide insights into the development of Ichinomiya in Kyushu, including relationships with the [[Dazaifu]] and the provincial office, and the trends in Kyushu during the 14th century. Senders include Seii Kokushi [[Enni]] (Saint Enni), who founded [[Tofukuji Temple]] in [[Kyoto]], and [[Imagawa Ryoshun]], the Kyushu Tandai. === Prefecture Designated === ==== Important Cultural Property ==== * West Gate - Designated on March 19, 1986{{Cite web|Japanese book|url=https://www.pref.saga.lg.jp/kiji0031451/index.html#jyu102|title=Saga Prefecture Important Cultural Property Yodohime Shrine West Gate|accessdate=2021.08.17|publisher=Saga Prefecture}}. : A [[Shikyakumon]] gate located to the northwest of the main hall, the ridge plaque copy in the Shoin documents states "Dedicated construction of the first shrine of Hizen Province Kawakami Yodohime Daimyojin West Gate by main sponsor Ryuzoji Taro Shiro Fujiwara no Ason Chikashi and Gonbu Danjo Daihitsu Takebe Nagayoshi. Constructed on an auspicious day in the third month of the fourth year of Genki (1573)". The roof is tiled, with Kirizuma-style, and the rafters are sparsely spaced. The gable has a frog decoration without carvings. The front and rear beams also have plain frog decorations, with the central bundle being rectangular. === City Designated === ==== Important Cultural Property ==== * Third Torii - Designated on October 17, 1983{{Cite web|Japanese book|url=https://www.city.saga.lg.jp/main/3887.html|title=Saga City Important Cultural Property P5|accessdate=2021.08.17|publisher=Saga City}}. : The inscription on the pillar reads "Constructed on an auspicious day in the mid-autumn of the 13th year of Keicho by Nabeshima Shinanokami Fujiwara no Ason Katsushige," indicating it was donated by Nabeshima Katsushige, the first lord of the [[Saga Domain]], in the 13th year of Keicho (1608). It is a stone Torii with a unique Hizen Torii style seen mainly in the Saga Prefecture area. Its characteristic features include three-part constructions for the Kasagi, Shimagi, Nuki, and pillars, with the Shimagi being a decorative element integrated with the Kasagi. == Others == Yodohime Shrine is designated as an Important Scenic Building in Saga City{{Cite web|Japanese book|url=https://www.city.saga.lg.jp/main/4769.html|title=Yodohime Shrine/Important Scenic Building|accessdate=2021.8.17|publisher=Saga City}}. Important Scenic Buildings in Saga City are those that have distinctive exterior features related to the region's nature, history, and culture, contributing to the formation of a favorable landscape, and are easily visible from public places such as roads{{Cite web|Japanese book|url=https://www.city.saga.lg.jp/main/333.html|title=Saga City Important Scenic Buildings|accessdate=2021.8.17|publisher=Saga City}}. == Legend == In this region, catfish are considered messengers of Yodohime-san (Yodohime-no-Mikoto) and are not eaten. The Hizen Fudoki's section on the god of Kawakami states, "Some people who fear the fish do not suffer, while others who catch and eat it die," and it is believed that this fish corresponds to the catfish in this area. == Front Gate Sweets == * Shiratama Manju - Originates from a legend related to the shrine. == Local Information == '''Location''' * [[Saga Prefecture]][[Saga City]] Yamatomachi Kawakami 1 '''Access''' * From [[JR Kyushu]] [[Nagasaki Main Line]] [[Saga Station]] ** Bus: [[Showa Bus]] to "Kawakami Bridge" bus stop (immediate walk after getting off) ** Car: About 20 minutes * Previously, there was a Hizen Kawakami Station, the terminus of the [[Saga Electric Railway]], across the Kase River. '''Nearby''' * [[Hizen Provincial Government Ruins]] * [[Funatsuka Burial Mound (Saga City)|Funatsuka Burial Mound]] - The largest keyhole-shaped burial mound in Saga Prefecture. == References == {{Reflist}} == Bibliography == * Shrine origin story * 'Japanese Historical Place Names Saga Prefecture Place Names' (Heibonsha) Saga District Kawakami Shrine section * [[Akira Sugitani]] 'Yodohime Shrine' (Edited by [[Kenichi Tanigawa]] 'Japanese Gods - Shrines and Sacred Sites - 1 Kyushu' (Hakusuisha)) == See also == * [[Chikushi Hachiman Shrine]] - Another shrine claiming to be Ichinomiya of Hizen Province. * [[Yodo Shrine]] * [[Tsukihi Shrine]] - A shrine in [[Nara City]] enshrining Yodohime-no-Mikoto. * [[Yoka Shrine]] - Enshrining Yodohime-no-Mikoto == External Links == {{Commonscat|Yodohime-jinja}} * [https://yodohime-jinja.jimdo.com/?logout=1/ Yodohime Shrine] (official site) * [http://www.sagabai.com/main/?cont=kanko&fid=57 Yodohime Shrine] (Saga City Tourism Association) {{Shinto Side}} {{DEFAULTSORT:Yodohime Shrine}} [[Category:Shrines in Saga Prefecture]] [[Category:Buildings and structures in Saga City]] [[Category:History of Saga City]] [[Category:Shikinai-sha of Hizen Province]] [[Category:Ichinomiya]] [[Category:Ken-sha]] [[Category:Uncategorized_Shinto_shrines]][[en:Yodohime Shrine]][[Category:Uncategorized_Shinto_shrines]] [[Category:Important Cultural Properties of Saga Prefecture]] [[Category:Hizen Province|Shrine1]] [[Category:Prefecture-designated Tangible Cultural Properties in Saga Prefecture]] [[Category:Municipal-designated Tangible Cultural Properties in Saga Prefecture]] ==History== ''Yodohime jinja'' was founded in the sixth century. Hizen Torii.]] '''Yodohime Shrine''' (Yodohime-jinja, also known as '''Yodohime Shrine''') is a [[shrine]] located in [[Saga Prefecture]], [[Saga City]]. It is a [[Shikinai-sha]], [[Ichinomiya]] of [[Hizen Province]], and a former [[Ken-sha]] under the modern shrine ranking system. It is also written as "Yodohime Shrine" and is also known as "'''Kawakami Shrine'''" and colloquially as "Yodohime-san." == History == === Founding === According to a fragment from the '[[Hizen Province Fudoki]]' (Shinmyocho Tochu), the god Yodohime was enshrined on November 1 in the 25th year of Emperor Kinmei (564?). It is said that Ayu fish and other fish swam upstream and dived near the northern part of Setahime Shrine, suggesting it was established as a water god worship from a river-related legend recorded in the same book'Gods of Japan' Yodohime Shrine section. === Historical Overview === In the 5th year of [[Engi (era name)|Engi]] (927), the '[[Engishiki]]' [[Engishiki Jinmyocho|Jinmyocho]] lists "Yodohime Shrine" in [[Saga District]], Hizen Province, and it was included among the [[Shikinai-sha]]. In the first year of [[Kochou]] (1260), it was granted the highest rank of Shoichii (Senior First Rank). In the [[Heian period]], Tajima-no-Kami Shrine (present-day [[Tajima Shrine]]) was revered as the god of safe voyages in Hizen Province and was ranked higher than Yodohime Shrine in the 'Jinmyocho', being the only Omiya in Hizen Province. However, after the medieval period, the actual status of Yodohime Shrine, which was closer to the provincial office, rose, and it was revered as Hizen Province's Ichinomiya. In the years of [[Oho]] (1161-1163), it became the Ichinomiya of Hizen Province, and in the first year of Kochou (1261), it received the Shoichii rank. However, as mentioned later, [[Chikushi Hachiman Shrine]] also claims to be Ichinomiya. During the [[Mongol invasions of Japan]] (1281), it is said that the godly spirit of Yodohime-no-Mikoto destroyed the enemy ships. In the 7th year of [[Keicho]] (1602), Emperor Go-Yozei personally bestowed a plaque inscribed with "Great Guardian of Japan's Western Region, Hizen Province's Great Protector, Shoichii Yodohime Daimyojin Ichinomiya" (preserved in the main hall: not open to the public). [[Hizen Province]] [[Ichinomiya]]

Hizen Torii.]] '''Yodohime Shrine''' (Yodohime-jinja, also known as '''Yodohime Shrine''') is a [[shrine]] located in [[Saga Prefecture]], [[Saga City]]. It is a [[Shikinai-sha]], [[Ichinomiya]] of [[Hizen Province]], and a former [[Ken-sha]] under the modern shrine ranking system. It is also written as "Yodohime Shrine" and is also known as "'''Kawakami Shrine'''" and colloquially as "Yodohime-san." == History == === Founding === According to a fragment from the '[[Hizen Province Fudoki]]' (Shinmyocho Tochu), the god Yodohime was enshrined on November 1 in the 25th year of Emperor Kinmei (564?). It is said that Ayu fish and other fish swam upstream and dived near the northern part of Setahime Shrine, suggesting it was established as a water god worship from a river-related legend recorded in the same book'Gods of Japan' Yodohime Shrine section. === Historical Overview === In the 5th year of [[Engi (era name)|Engi]] (927), the '[[Engishiki]]' [[Engishiki Jinmyocho|Jinmyocho]] lists "Yodohime Shrine" in [[Saga District]], Hizen Province, and it was included among the [[Shikinai-sha]]. In the first year of [[Kochou]] (1260), it was granted the highest rank of Shoichii (Senior First Rank). In the [[Heian period]], Tajima-no-Kami Shrine (present-day [[Tajima Shrine]]) was revered as the god of safe voyages in Hizen Province and was ranked higher than Yodohime Shrine in the 'Jinmyocho', being the only Omiya in Hizen Province. However, after the medieval period, the actual status of Yodohime Shrine, which was closer to the provincial office, rose, and it was revered as Hizen Province's Ichinomiya. In the years of [[Oho]] (1161-1163), it became the Ichinomiya of Hizen Province, and in the first year of Kochou (1261), it received the Shoichii rank. However, as mentioned later, [[Chikushi Hachiman Shrine]] also claims to be Ichinomiya. During the [[Mongol invasions of Japan]] (1281), it is said that the godly spirit of Yodohime-no-Mikoto destroyed the enemy ships. In the 7th year of [[Keicho]] (1602), Emperor Go-Yozei personally bestowed a plaque inscribed with "Great Guardian of Japan's Western Region, Hizen Province's Great Protector, Shoichii Yodohime Daimyojin Ichinomiya" (preserved in the main hall: not open to the public). This confirms that Yodohime Shrine was recognized as the Ichinomiya of Hizen Province, leading to a 60-year dispute with Chikushi Hachiman Shrine over the title. According to old records, the main hall, Heiden, and Haiden were burned down in the 10th year of Bunka (1813) and rebuilt by the Nabeshima family in the 13th year of Bunka (1816). In the 4th year of [[Meiji]] (1871), it was classified as a [[Ken-sha]] under the modern shrine ranking system. There were plans for its elevation to a Kokuheisha, but these were not realized due to the end of [[World War II]]. === Divine Rank === * Six National Histories ** [[Jogan (Japan)|Jogan]] 2nd year (860) February 8th, from Jugoi-no-ge to Jugoi-no-jo ( '[[Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku]]') - Written as "Yodohime Tenjin". ** Jogan 15th year (873) September 16th, Shogoi-no-ge ( 'Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku') - Written as "Yodohime no Kami". * Kochou first year (1260), Shoichii == Deities == * '''Yodohime-no-Mikoto''' *: Said to be the sister of [[Empress Jingu]]. Another theory states she is [[Toyotama-hime]]Deities according to the shrine's origin story.. *: In a fragment of the '[[Hizen Province Fudoki]]' (Shinmyocho Tochu), it is stated that the alternate names for "Yodohime no Kami" are "Toyohime" and "Yodohime". Another section of the same book in Saga District includes the story of "Setahime," suggesting they are the same deity'Saga Prefecture Place Names' Kawakami Shrine section.. There are many shrines dedicated to Yodohime (Yodohime no Kami) in northern Kyushu, centered around Saga Prefecture, with six of them, including this shrine, located along the [[Kase River]]. == Shrine Grounds == * First Torii (located outside the grounds) * Second Torii * Third Torii - '''Hizen Torii''': City-designated Important Cultural Property * West Gate - Prefecture-designated Important Cultural Property * Haiden, Chuden, Main Hall : Haiden: Five bays in front, three bays on the side, Irimoya-zukuri, Karahafu-style, with a separate Shinsenjo :Chuden: One bay in front, four bays on the side :Main Hall: Five-bay Nagare-zukuri, four bays on the side * Enshrined Shrine Yodohime Tenmangu The shrine grounds are located on the right bank of the [[Kase River]]. The West Gate, built in the 4th year of [[Genki]] (1573), is a prefecture-designated Important Cultural Property, while the third Torii, built in the 13th year of [[Keicho]] (1608), is a city-designated Important Cultural Property. The first Torii stands near Tateishi Intersection ({{Coord|33|18|28.75|N|130|15|50.15|E|region:JP-41_type:landmark|name=First Torii}}). Inside the Haiden are ceiling paintings, Thirty-Six Immortal Poets plaques, and dedication plaques. The ceiling paintings consist of 250 pieces from two scrolls: "The Tale of Yamasachihiko and Umisachihiko," relating to the deity Toyotama-hime, and the "Tale of Sugawara no Michizane," related to the enshrined deity Tenmangu. The Thirty-Six Immortal Poets plaques feature portraits of renowned poets from the Heian period with one of their representative poems. The original Thirty-Six Immortal Poets plaques, which were dedicated in the late Edo period, had deteriorated and were repainted and rededicated in 2015. Both the ceiling paintings and the Thirty-Six Immortal Poets plaques were created by the painter Yin Yusheng, who resides in Saga City and is originally from [[Dalian City]], [[China]]According to local information board. File:Yodohime-jinja honden.JPG|Main Hall File:Yodohime-jinja shaden.JPG|Haiden File:Yodohime-jinja nishimon.JPG|West Gate (Prefecture-designated Cultural Property) File:Yodohime Shrine Tenman-gu.jpg|Enshrined Shrine Yodohime Tenmangu File:Yodohime-jinja ninotorii.JPG|Second Torii File:Yodohime-jinja ichinotorii.JPG|First Torii == Annual Festivals == * Spring Festival (April 18) * Autumn Festival (October 10) * Niiname-sai (December 18) == Cultural Properties == === Nationally Designated === ==== Important Cultural Property ==== * 14 volumes of Kawakami Shrine Documents (247 items) : 10 items from the Heian period, 92 items from the Kamakura period, 85 items from the [[Nanboku-cho period]], 57 items from the Muromachi period, 3 items from the Azuchi-Momoyama period. Designated on June 6, 1980{{Cite web|Japanese book|url=https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/201/9051|title=Kawakami Shrine Documents (247 items)／Nationally Designated Cultural Property Database|accessdate=2021.08.17|publisher=Agency for Cultural Affairs}}. Deposited at the [[Saga Prefectural Library]]. :The oldest item among these is the Shazo Enjin Resolution from the 5th year of Kanji (1091){{Cite web|Japanese book|url=http://yodohime.area9.jp/category/0140122.html|title=Brief History of Hizen Ichinomiya Yodohime Shrine|accessdate=2021.08.17|publisher=Yodohime Shrine Official}}. These documents provide insights into the development of Ichinomiya in Kyushu, including relationships with the [[Dazaifu]] and the provincial office, and the trends in Kyushu during the 14th century. Senders include Seii Kokushi [[Enni]] (Saint Enni), who founded [[Tofukuji Temple]] in [[Kyoto]], and [[Imagawa Ryoshun]], the Kyushu Tandai. === Prefecture Designated === ==== Important Cultural Property ==== * West Gate - Designated on March 19, 1986{{Cite web|Japanese book|url=https://www.pref.saga.lg.jp/kiji0031451/index.html#jyu102|title=Saga Prefecture Important Cultural Property Yodohime Shrine West Gate|accessdate=2021.08.17|publisher=Saga Prefecture}}. : A [[Shikyakumon]] gate located to the northwest of the main hall, the ridge plaque copy in the Shoin documents states "Dedicated construction of the first shrine of Hizen Province Kawakami Yodohime Daimyojin West Gate by main sponsor Ryuzoji Taro Shiro Fujiwara no Ason Chikashi and Gonbu Danjo Daihitsu Takebe Nagayoshi. Constructed on an auspicious day in the third month of the fourth year of Genki (1573)". The roof is tiled, with Kirizuma-style, and the rafters are sparsely spaced. The gable has a frog decoration without carvings. The front and rear beams also have plain frog decorations, with the central bundle being rectangular. === City Designated === ==== Important Cultural Property ==== * Third Torii - Designated on October 17, 1983{{Cite web|Japanese book|url=https://www.city.saga.lg.jp/main/3887.html|title=Saga City Important Cultural Property P5|accessdate=2021.08.17|publisher=Saga City}}. : The inscription on the pillar reads "Constructed on an auspicious day in the mid-autumn of the 13th year of Keicho by Nabeshima Shinanokami Fujiwara no Ason Katsushige," indicating it was donated by Nabeshima Katsushige, the first lord of the [[Saga Domain]], in the 13th year of Keicho (1608). It is a stone Torii with a unique Hizen Torii style seen mainly in the Saga Prefecture area. Its characteristic features include three-part constructions for the Kasagi, Shimagi, Nuki, and pillars, with the Shimagi being a decorative element integrated with the Kasagi. == Others == Yodohime Shrine is designated as an Important Scenic Building in Saga City{{Cite web|Japanese book|url=https://www.city.saga.lg.jp/main/4769.html|title=Yodohime Shrine/Important Scenic Building|accessdate=2021.8.17|publisher=Saga City}}. Important Scenic Buildings in Saga City are those that have distinctive exterior features related to the region's nature, history, and culture, contributing to the formation of a favorable landscape, and are easily visible from public places such as roads{{Cite web|Japanese book|url=https://www.city.saga.lg.jp/main/333.html|title=Saga City Important Scenic Buildings|accessdate=2021.8.17|publisher=Saga City}}. == Legend == In this region, catfish are considered messengers of Yodohime-san (Yodohime-no-Mikoto) and are not eaten. The Hizen Fudoki's section on the god of Kawakami states, "Some people who fear the fish do not suffer, while others who catch and eat it die," and it is believed that this fish corresponds to the catfish in this area. == Front Gate Sweets == * Shiratama Manju - Originates from a legend related to the shrine. == Local Information == '''Location''' * [[Saga Prefecture]][[Saga City]] Yamatomachi Kawakami 1 '''Access''' * From [[JR Kyushu]] [[Nagasaki Main Line]] [[Saga Station]] ** Bus: [[Showa Bus]] to "Kawakami Bridge" bus stop (immediate walk after getting off) ** Car: About 20 minutes * Previously, there was a Hizen Kawakami Station, the terminus of the [[Saga Electric Railway]], across the Kase River. '''Nearby''' * [[Hizen Provincial Government Ruins]] * [[Funatsuka Burial Mound (Saga City)|Funatsuka Burial Mound]] - The largest keyhole-shaped burial mound in Saga Prefecture. == References == {{Reflist}} == Bibliography == * Shrine origin story * 'Japanese Historical Place Names Saga Prefecture Place Names' (Heibonsha) Saga District Kawakami Shrine section * [[Akira Sugitani]] 'Yodohime Shrine' (Edited by [[Kenichi Tanigawa]] 'Japanese Gods - Shrines and Sacred Sites - 1 Kyushu' (Hakusuisha)) == See also == * [[Chikushi Hachiman Shrine]] - Another shrine claiming to be Ichinomiya of Hizen Province. * [[Yodo Shrine]] * [[Tsukihi Shrine]] - A shrine in [[Nara City]] enshrining Yodohime-no-Mikoto. * [[Yoka Shrine]] - Enshrining Yodohime-no-Mikoto == External Links == {{Commonscat|Yodohime-jinja}} * [https://yodohime-jinja.jimdo.com/?logout=1/ Yodohime Shrine] (official site) * [http://www.sagabai.com/main/?cont=kanko&fid=57 Yodohime Shrine] (Saga City Tourism Association) {{Shinto Side}} {{DEFAULTSORT:Yodohime Shrine}} [[Category:Shrines in Saga Prefecture]] [[Category:Buildings and structures in Saga City]] [[Category:History of Saga City]] [[Category:Shikinai-sha of Hizen Province]] [[Category:Ichinomiya]] [[Category:Ken-sha]] [[en:Yodohime Shrine]][[Category:Important Cultural Properties of Saga Prefecture]] [[Category:Hizen Province|Shrine1]] [[Category:Prefecture-designated Tangible Cultural Properties in Saga Prefecture]] [[Category:Municipal-designated Tangible Cultural Properties in Saga Prefecture]] ==History== ''Yodohime jinja'' was founded in the sixth century. It enshrines the ''[[kami]]'' of the grandmother of [[Emperor Jimmu]]. It was one of two chief [[Shinto shrine]] (''[[ichinomiya]]'') of [[Hizen Province]] and Saga Prefecture.Picken, Stuart. (2004). [https://books.google.com/books?id=v7Xs1NzMMHMC&pg=PA377 ''Sourcebook in Shinto: Selected Documents,'' p. 377]; [http://eos.kokugakuin.ac.jp/modules/xwords/images/uploads/EOS070712Ab.pdf "Nationwide List of ''Ichinomiya''," p. 3] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130517061440/http://eos.kokugakuin.ac.jp/modules/xwords/images/uploads/EOS070712Ab.pdf |date=2013-05-17 }}; retrieved 2012-8-23. ==References== {{Reflist}} ==Other websites== {{Commons category-inline|Yodohime-jinja}} * [http://yodohime.area9.jp/ Yodohime jinja website {{in lang|ja}}] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121114185918/http://yodohime.area9.jp/ |date=2012-11-14 }} {{coord|33|32|N|130|26|E|scale:500000|display=title}} {{Japan-stub}} {{DEFAULTSORT:Yodohime jinja}} [[Category:Shinto shrines in Saga Prefecture]] [[Category:6th-century establishments in Asia]] [[Category:Ichinomiya]] [[Category:Fuken-sha]] [[Category:[[Category:Original pages]] [[ja:與止日女神社]] [[simple:Yodohime Shrine]] [[en:Yodohime Shrine]] ]]
