Hizen Torii.]] '''Yodohime Shrine''' (Yodohime-jinja, also known as '''Yodohime Shrine''') is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en|Shinto shrine|WD=Q845945|lt=shrine}} located in {{ill|Saga Prefecture|en|Saga Prefecture|WD=Q160420|lt=Saga Prefecture}}, [[:en:Saga City|Saga City]]. It is a {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|ja|延喜式神名帳|lt=Shikinaisha}}, [[Ichinomiya]] of {{ill|Hizen Province|en|Hizen Province|WD=Q906926|lt=Hizen Province}}, and a former [[Ken-sha]] under the modern shrine Ranking system. It is also written as "Yodohime Shrine" and is also known as "'''Kawakami Shrine'''" and colloquially as "Yodohime-san." == History == === Founding === According to a fragment from the '[[Hizen Province Fudoki]]' (Shinmyocho Tochu), the god Yodohime was enshrined on November 1 in the 25th year of Emperor Kinmei (564?). It is said that Ayu fish and other fish swam upstream and dived near the northern part of Setahime Shrine, suggesting it was established as a water god worship from a river-related legend recorded in the same book'Gods of Japan' Yodohime Shrine section. === Historical Overview === In the 5th year of [[Engi (era name)|Engi]] (927), the '[[Engishiki]]' [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|Jinmyocho]] lists "Yodohime Shrine" in [[Saga District]], Hizen Province, and it was included among the {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|ja|延喜式神名帳|lt=Shikinaisha}}. In the first year of [[Kochou]] (1260), it was granted the highest Rank of Shoichii (Senior First Rank). In the {{ill|Heian period|en|Heian period|WD=Q193292|lt=Heian period}}, Tajima-no-Kami Shrine (present-day [[Tajima Shrine]]) was revered as the god of safe voyages in Hizen Province and was Ranked higher than Yodohime Shrine in the 'Jinmyocho', being the only Omiya in Hizen Province. However, after the medieval period, the actual status of Yodohime Shrine, which was closer to the provincial office, rose, and it was revered as Hizen Province's Ichinomiya. In the years of {{ill|Oho|en|Oho|WD=Q7081125|lt=Oho}} (1161-1163), it became the Ichinomiya of Hizen Province, and in the first year of Kochou (1261), it received the Shoichii Rank. However, as mentioned later, [[Chikushi Hachiman Shrine]] also claims to be Ichinomiya. During the {{ill|Mongol invasions of Japan|en|Mongol invasions of Japan|WD=Q208156|lt=Mongol invasions of Japan}} (1281), it is said that the godly spirit of Yodohime-no-Mikoto destroyed the enemy ships. In the 7th year of [[:en:Keicho|Keicho]] (1602), Emperor Go-Yozei personally bestowed a plaque inscribed with "Great Guardian of Japan's Western Region, Hizen Province's Great Protector, Shoichii Yodohime Daimyojin Ichinomiya" (preserved in the main hall: not open to the public). This confirms that Yodohime Shrine was recognized as the Ichinomiya of Hizen Province, leading to a 60-year dispute with Chikushi Hachiman Shrine over the title. According to old records, the main hall, Heiden, and Haiden were burned down in the 10th year of Bunka (1813) and rebuilt by the Nabeshima family in the 13th year of Bunka (1816). In the 4th year of [[Meiji]] (1871), it was classified as a [[Ken-sha]] under the modern shrine Ranking system. There were plans for its elevation to a Kokuheisha, but these were not realized due to the end of {{ill|Pacific War|en|Pacific War|WD=Q184425|lt=Pacific War}}. === Divine Rank === * Six National Histories ** [[Jogan (Japan)|Jogan]] 2nd year (860) February 8th, from Jugoi-no-ge to Jugoi-no-jo ( '[[Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku]]') - Written as "Yodohime Tenjin". ** Jogan 15th year (873) September 16th, Shogoi-no-ge ( 'Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku') - Written as "Yodohime no Kami". * Kochou first year (1260), Shoichii == Deities == * '''Yodohime-no-Mikoto''' *: Said to be the sister of {{ill|Empress Jingū|en|Empress Jingū|WD=Q232803|lt=Empress Jingū}}. Another theory states she is {{ill|Toyotama-hime|en|Toyotama-hime|WD=Q2329261|lt=Toyotama-hime}}Deities according to the shrine's origin story.. *: In a fragment of the '[[Hizen Province Fudoki]]' (Shinmyocho Tochu), it is stated that the alternate names for "Yodohime no Kami" are "Toyohime" and "Yodohime". Another section of the same book in Saga District includes the story of "Setahime," suggesting they are the same deity'Saga Prefecture Place names' Kawakami Shrine section.. There are many shrines dedicated to Yodohime (Yodohime no Kami) in northern Kyushu, centered around Saga Prefecture, with six of them, including this shrine, located along the [[Kase River]]. == Shrine Grounds == * First Torii (located outside the grounds) * Second Torii * Third Torii * '''Hizen Torii''': City-designated Important Cultural Property * West Gate - Prefecture-designated Important Cultural Property * Haiden, Chuden, main hall : Haiden: Five bays in front, three bays on the side, Irimoya-zukuri, Karahafu-style, with a separate Shinsenjo :Chuden: One bay in front, four bays on the side :main hall: Five-bay Nagare-zukuri, four bays on the side * Enshrined Shrine Yodohime Tenmangu The shrine grounds are located on the right bank of the [[Kase River]]. The West Gate, built in the 4th year of {{ill|Genki|en|Genki|WD=Q21501757|lt=Genki}} (1573), is a prefecture-designated Important Cultural Property, while the third Torii, built in the 13th year of [[:en:Keicho|Keicho]] (1608), is a city-designated Important Cultural Property. The first Torii stands near Tateishi Intersection ({{Coord|33|18|28.75|N|130|15|50.15|E|region:JP-41_type:landmark|name=First Torii}}). Inside the Haiden are ceiling paintings, Thirty-Six Immortal Poets plaques, and dedication plaques. The ceiling paintings consist of 250 pieces from two scrolls: "The Tale of Yamasachihiko and Umisachihiko," relating to the deity Toyotama-hime, and the "Tale of Sugawara no Michizane," related to the enshrined deity Tenmangu. The Thirty-Six Immortal Poets plaques feature portraits of renowned poets from the Heian period with one of their representative poems. The original Thirty-Six Immortal Poets plaques, which were dedicated in the late Edo period, had deteriorated and were repainted and rededicated in 2015. Both the ceiling paintings and the Thirty-Six Immortal Poets plaques were created by the painter Yin Yusheng, who resides in Saga City and is originally from [[:en:Dalian City|Dalian City]], {{ill|China|en|China|WD=Q148|lt=China}}According to local information board. Designated on June 6, 1980{{Cite web|Japanese book|url=https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/201/9051|title=Kawakami Shrine Documents (247 items)／Nationally Designated Cultural Property Database|accessdate=2021.08.17|publisher=Agency for Cultural Affairs}}. These documents provide insights into the development of Ichinomiya in Kyushu, including relationships with the {{ill|Dazaifu|en|Dazaifu|WD=Q1179277|lt=Dazaifu}} and the provincial office, and the trends in Kyushu during the 14th century. Senders include Seii Kokushi {{ill|Enni|en|Enni|WD=Q739826|lt=Enni}} (Saint Enni), who founded [[Tofukuji Temple]] in {{ill|Kyoto|en|Kyoto|WD=Q34600|lt=Kyoto}}, and [[:en:Imagawa Ryoshun|Imagawa Ryoshun]], the Kyushu Tandai. === Prefecture Designated === ==== Important Cultural Property ==== * West Gate - Designated on March 19, 1986{{Cite web|Japanese book|url=https://www.pref.saga.lg.jp/kiji0031451/index.html#jyu102|title=Saga Prefecture Important Cultural Property Yodohime Shrine West Gate|accessdate=2021.08.17|publisher=Saga Prefecture}}. : A [[Shikyakumon]] gate located to the northwest of the main hall, the ridge plaque copy in the Shoin documents states "Dedicated construction of the first shrine of Hizen Province Kawakami Yodohime Daimyojin West Gate by main sponsor Ryuzoji Taro Shiro Fujiwara no Ason Chikashi and Gonbu Danjo Daihitsu Takebe Nagayoshi. Constructed on an auspicious day in the third month of the fourth year of Genki (1573)". The roof is tiled, with Kirizuma-style, and the rafters are sparsely spaced. The gable has a frog decoration without carvings. The front and rear beams also have plain frog decorations, with the central bundle being rectangular. === City Designated === ==== Important Cultural Property ==== * Third Torii - Designated on October 17, 1983{{Cite web|Japanese book|url=https://www.city.saga.lg.jp/main/3887.html|title=Saga City Important Cultural Property P5|accessdate=2021.08.17|publisher=Saga City}}. : The inscription on the pillar reads "Constructed on an auspicious day in the mid-autumn of the 13th year of Keicho by Nabeshima Shinanokami Fujiwara no Ason Katsushige," indicating it was donated by Nabeshima Katsushige, the first lord of the {{ill|Saga Domain|en|Saga Domain|WD=Q2975995|lt=Saga Domain}}, in the 13th year of Keicho (1608). It is a stone Torii with a unique Hizen Torii style seen mainly in the Saga Prefecture area. Its characteristic features include three-part constructions for the Kasagi, Shimagi, Nuki, and pillars, with the Shimagi being a decorative element integrated with the Kasagi. == Others == Yodohime Shrine is designated as an Important Scenic Building in Saga City{{Cite web|Japanese book|url=https://www.city.saga.lg.jp/main/4769.html|title=Yodohime Shrine/Important Scenic Building|accessdate=2021.8.17|publisher=Saga City}}. It is a {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|ja|延喜式神名帳|lt=Shikinaisha}}, [[Ichinomiya]] of {{ill|Hizen Province|en|Hizen Province|WD=Q906926|lt=Hizen Province}}, and a former [[Ken-sha]] under the modern shrine Ranking system. It is also written as "Yodohime Shrine" and is also known as "'''Kawakami Shrine'''" and colloquially as "Yodohime-san." == History == === Founding === According to a fragment from the '[[Hizen Province Fudoki]]' (Shinmyocho Tochu), the god Yodohime was enshrined on November 1 in the 25th year of Emperor Kinmei (564?). It is said that Ayu fish and other fish swam upstream and dived near the northern part of Setahime Shrine, suggesting it was established as a water god worship from a river-related legend recorded in the same book'Gods of Japan' Yodohime Shrine section. === Historical Overview === In the 5th year of [[Engi (era name)|Engi]] (927), the '[[Engishiki]]' [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|Jinmyocho]] lists "Yodohime Shrine" in [[Saga District]], Hizen Province, and it was included among the {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|ja|延喜式神名帳|lt=Shikinaisha}}. In the first year of [[Kochou]] (1260), it was granted the highest Rank of Shoichii (Senior First Rank). In the {{ill|Heian period|en|Heian period|WD=Q193292|lt=Heian period}}, Tajima-no-Kami Shrine (present-day [[Tajima Shrine]]) was revered as the god of safe voyages in Hizen Province and was Ranked higher than Yodohime Shrine in the 'Jinmyocho', being the only Omiya in Hizen Province. However, after the medieval period, the actual status of Yodohime Shrine, which was closer to the provincial office, rose, and it was revered as Hizen Province's Ichinomiya. In the years of {{ill|Oho|en|Oho|WD=Q7081125|lt=Oho}} (1161-1163), it became the Ichinomiya of Hizen Province, and in the first year of Kochou (1261), it received the Shoichii Rank. However, as mentioned later, [[Chikushi Hachiman Shrine]] also claims to be Ichinomiya. During the {{ill|Mongol invasions of Japan|en|Mongol invasions of Japan|WD=Q208156|lt=Mongol invasions of Japan}} (1281), it is said that the godly spirit of Yodohime-no-Mikoto destroyed the enemy ships. In the 7th year of [[:en:Keicho|Keicho]] (1602), Emperor Go-Yozei personally bestowed a plaque inscribed with "Great Guardian of Japan's Western Region, Hizen Province's Great Protector, Shoichii Yodohime Daimyojin Ichinomiya" (preserved in the main hall: not open to the public). This confirms that Yodohime Shrine was recognized as the Ichinomiya of Hizen Province, leading to a 60-year dispute with Chikushi Hachiman Shrine over the title. According to old records, the main hall, Heiden, and Haiden were burned down in the 10th year of Bunka (1813) and rebuilt by the Nabeshima family in the 13th year of Bunka (1816). In the 4th year of [[Meiji]] (1871), it was classified as a [[Ken-sha]] under the modern shrine Ranking system. There were plans for its elevation to a Kokuheisha, but these were not realized due to the end of {{ill|Pacific War|en|Pacific War|WD=Q184425|lt=Pacific War}}. === Divine Rank === * Six National Histories ** [[Jogan (Japan)|Jogan]] 2nd year (860) February 8th, from Jugoi-no-ge to Jugoi-no-jo ( '[[Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku]]') - Written as "Yodohime Tenjin". ** Jogan 15th year (873) September 16th, Shogoi-no-ge ( 'Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku') - Written as "Yodohime no Kami". * Kochou first year (1260), Shoichii == Deities == * '''Yodohime-no-Mikoto''' *: Said to be the sister of {{ill|Empress Jingū|en|Empress Jingū|WD=Q232803|lt=Empress Jingū}}. Another theory states she is {{ill|Toyotama-hime|en|Toyotama-hime|WD=Q2329261|lt=Toyotama-hime}}Deities according to the shrine's origin story.. *: In a fragment of the '[[Hizen Province Fudoki]]' (Shinmyocho Tochu), it is stated that the alternate names for "Yodohime no Kami" are "Toyohime" and "Yodohime". Another section of the same book in Saga District includes the story of "Setahime," suggesting they are the same deity'Saga Prefecture Place names' Kawakami Shrine section.. There are many shrines dedicated to Yodohime (Yodohime no Kami) in northern Kyushu, centered around Saga Prefecture, with six of them, including this shrine, located along the [[Kase River]]. == Shrine Grounds == * First Torii (located outside the grounds) * Second Torii * Third Torii * '''Hizen Torii''': City-designated Important Cultural Property * West Gate - Prefecture-designated Important Cultural Property * Haiden, Chuden, main hall : Haiden: Five bays in front, three bays on the side, Irimoya-zukuri, Karahafu-style, with a separate Shinsenjo :Chuden: One bay in front, four bays on the side :main hall: Five-bay Nagare-zukuri, four bays on the side * Enshrined Shrine Yodohime Tenmangu The shrine grounds are located on the right bank of the [[Kase River]]. The West Gate, built in the 4th year of {{ill|Genki|en|Genki|WD=Q21501757|lt=Genki}} (1573), is a prefecture-designated Important Cultural Property, while the third Torii, built in the 13th year of [[:en:Keicho|Keicho]] (1608), is a city-designated Important Cultural Property. The first Torii stands near Tateishi Intersection ({{Coord|33|18|28.75|N|130|15|50.15|E|region:JP-41_type:landmark|name=First Torii}}). Inside the Haiden are ceiling paintings, Thirty-Six Immortal Poets plaques, and dedication plaques. The ceiling paintings consist of 250 pieces from two scrolls: "The Tale of Yamasachihiko and Umisachihiko," relating to the deity Toyotama-hime, and the "Tale of Sugawara no Michizane," related to the enshrined deity Tenmangu. The Thirty-Six Immortal Poets plaques feature portraits of renowned poets from the Heian period with one of their representative poems. The original Thirty-Six Immortal Poets plaques, which were dedicated in the late Edo period, had deteriorated and were repainted and rededicated in 2015. Both the ceiling paintings and the Thirty-Six Immortal Poets plaques were created by the painter Yin Yusheng, who resides in Saga City and is originally from [[:en:Dalian City|Dalian City]], {{ill|China|en|China|WD=Q148|lt=China}}According to local information board. File:Yodohime-jinja honden.JPG|main hall File:Yodohime-jinja shaden.JPG|Haiden File:Yodohime-jinja nishimon.JPG|West Gate (Prefecture-designated Cultural Property) File:Yodohime Shrine Tenman-gu.jpg|Enshrined Shrine Yodohime Tenmangu File:Yodohime-jinja ninotorii.JPG|Second Torii File:Yodohime-jinja ichinotorii.JPG|First Torii == festivals == * Spring festival (April 18) * Autumn festival (October 10) * Niiname-sai (December 18) == Cultural Properties == === Nationally Designated === ==== Important Cultural Property ==== * 14 volumes of Kawakami Shrine Documents (247 items) : 10 items from the Heian period, 92 items from the Kamakura period, 85 items from the {{ill|Nanboku-chō period|en|Nanboku-chō period|WD=Q264012|lt=Nanboku-chō period}}, 57 items from the Muromachi period, 3 items from the Azuchi-Momoyama period. Designated on June 6, 1980{{Cite web|Japanese book|url=https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/201/9051|title=Kawakami Shrine Documents (247 items)／Nationally Designated Cultural Property Database|accessdate=2021.08.17|publisher=Agency for Cultural Affairs}}. Deposited at the [[Saga Prefectural Library]]. :The oldest item among these is the Shazo Enjin Resolution from the 5th year of Kanji (1091){{Cite web|Japanese book|url=http://yodohime.area9.jp/category/0140122.html|title=Brief History of Hizen Ichinomiya Yodohime Shrine|accessdate=2021.08.17|publisher=Yodohime Shrine Official}}. These documents provide insights into the development of Ichinomiya in Kyushu, including relationships with the {{ill|Dazaifu|en|Dazaifu|WD=Q1179277|lt=Dazaifu}} and the provincial office, and the trends in Kyushu during the 14th century. Senders include Seii Kokushi {{ill|Enni|en|Enni|WD=Q739826|lt=Enni}} (Saint Enni), who founded [[Tofukuji Temple]] in {{ill|Kyoto|en|Kyoto|WD=Q34600|lt=Kyoto}}, and [[:en:Imagawa Ryoshun|Imagawa Ryoshun]], the Kyushu Tandai. === Prefecture Designated === ==== Important Cultural Property ==== * West Gate - Designated on March 19, 1986{{Cite web|Japanese book|url=https://www.pref.saga.lg.jp/kiji0031451/index.html#jyu102|title=Saga Prefecture Important Cultural Property Yodohime Shrine West Gate|accessdate=2021.08.17|publisher=Saga Prefecture}}. : A [[Shikyakumon]] gate located to the northwest of the main hall, the ridge plaque copy in the Shoin documents states "Dedicated construction of the first shrine of Hizen Province Kawakami Yodohime Daimyojin West Gate by main sponsor Ryuzoji Taro Shiro Fujiwara no Ason Chikashi and Gonbu Danjo Daihitsu Takebe Nagayoshi. Constructed on an auspicious day in the third month of the fourth year of Genki (1573)". The roof is tiled, with Kirizuma-style, and the rafters are sparsely spaced. The gable has a frog decoration without carvings. The front and rear beams also have plain frog decorations, with the central bundle being rectangular. === City Designated === ==== Important Cultural Property ==== * Third Torii - Designated on October 17, 1983{{Cite web|Japanese book|url=https://www.city.saga.lg.jp/main/3887.html|title=Saga City Important Cultural Property P5|accessdate=2021.08.17|publisher=Saga City}}. : The inscription on the pillar reads "Constructed on an auspicious day in the mid-autumn of the 13th year of Keicho by Nabeshima Shinanokami Fujiwara no Ason Katsushige," indicating it was donated by Nabeshima Katsushige, the first lord of the {{ill|Saga Domain|en|Saga Domain|WD=Q2975995|lt=Saga Domain}}, in the 13th year of Keicho (1608). It is a stone Torii with a unique Hizen Torii style seen mainly in the Saga Prefecture area. Its characteristic features include three-part constructions for the Kasagi, Shimagi, Nuki, and pillars, with the Shimagi being a decorative element integrated with the Kasagi. == Others == Yodohime Shrine is designated as an Important Scenic Building in Saga City{{Cite web|Japanese book|url=https://www.city.saga.lg.jp/main/4769.html|title=Yodohime Shrine/Important Scenic Building|accessdate=2021.8.17|publisher=Saga City}}. Important Scenic Buildings in Saga City are those that have distinctive exterior features related to the region's nature, history, and culture, contributing to the formation of a favorable landscape, and are easily visible from public places such as roads{{Cite web|Japanese book|url=https://www.city.saga.lg.jp/main/333.html|title=Saga City Important Scenic Buildings|accessdate=2021.8.17|publisher=Saga City}}. == Legend == In this region, catfish are considered messengers of Yodohime-san (Yodohime-no-Mikoto) and are not eaten. The Hizen Fudoki's section on the god of Kawakami states, "Some people who fear the fish do not suffer, while others who catch and eat it die," and it is believed that this fish corresponds to the catfish in this area. == Front Gate Sweets == * Shiratama Manju - Originates from a legend related to the shrine. == Local Information == '''location''' * {{ill|Saga Prefecture|en|Saga Prefecture|WD=Q160420|lt=Saga Prefecture}}[[:en:Saga City|Saga City]] Yamatomachi Kawakami 1 '''Access''' * From {{ill|Kyushu Railway Company|en|Kyushu Railway Company|WD=Q498366|lt=Kyushu Railway Company}} {{ill|Nagasaki Main Line|en|Nagasaki Main Line|WD=Q1078117|lt=Nagasaki Main Line}} {{ill|Saga Station|en|Saga Station|WD=Q1042665|lt=Saga Station}} ** Bus: [[Showa Bus]] to "Kawakami Bridge" bus stop (immediate walk after getting off) ** Car: About 20 minutes * Previously, there was a Hizen Kawakami Station, the terminus of the [[Saga Electric Railway]], across the Kase River. '''Nearby''' * [[Hizen Provincial Government Ruins]] * [[Funatsuka Kofun (Saga City)|Funatsuka Kofun]] - The largest keyhole-shaped Kofun in Saga Prefecture. == References == {{Reflist}} == Bibliography == * Shrine origin story * 'Japanese Historical Place names Saga Prefecture Place names' (Heibonsha) Saga District Kawakami Shrine section * [[Akira Sugitani]] 'Yodohime Shrine' (Edited by [[Kenichi Tanigawa]] 'Japanese Gods - Shrines and Sacred Sites - 1 Kyushu' (Hakusuisha)) == See also == * [[Chikushi Hachiman Shrine]] - Another shrine claiming to be Ichinomiya of Hizen Province. * [[Yodo Shrine]] * [[Tsukihi Shrine]] - A shrine in [[:en:Nara City|Nara City]] enshrining Yodohime-no-Mikoto. * [[Yoka Shrine]] - Enshrining Yodohime-no-Mikoto == External Links == {{Commonscat|Yodohime-jinja}} * [https://yodohime-jinja.jimdo.com/?logout=1/ Yodohime Shrine] (official site) * [http://www.sagabai.com/main/?cont=kanko&fid=57 Yodohime Shrine] (Saga City Tourism Association) {{Shinto shrines}} ==History== ''Yodohime jinja'' was founded in the sixth century. It enshrines the ''[[kami]]'' of the grandmother of {{ill|Emperor Jimmu|en|Emperor Jimmu|WD=Q200188|lt=Emperor Jimmu}}. It was one of two chief {{ill|Shinto shrine|en|Shinto shrine|WD=Q845945|lt=Shinto shrine}} (''[[ichinomiya]]'') of {{ill|Hizen Province|en|Hizen Province|WD=Q906926|lt=Hizen Province}} and Saga Prefecture.Picken, Stuart. (2004). [https://books.google.com/books?id=v7Xs1NzMMHMC&pg=PA377 ''Sourcebook in Shinto: Selected Documents,'' p. 377]; [http://eos.kokugakuin.ac.jp/modules/xwords/images/uploads/EOS070712Ab.pdf "Nationwide List of ''Ichinomiya''," p. 3] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130517061440/http://eos.kokugakuin.ac.jp/modules/xwords/images/uploads/EOS070712Ab.pdf |date=2013-05-17 }}; retrieved 2012-8-23. ==References== {{Reflist}} ==Other websites== {{Commons category-inline|Yodohime-jinja}} * [http://yodohime.area9.jp/ Yodohime jinja website {{in lang|ja}]] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121114185918/http://yodohime.area9.jp/ |date=2012-11-14 }} {{coord|33|32|N|130|26|E|scale:500000|display=title}} {{Japan-stub}} {{Ichinomiya}} {{translated page|ja|與止日女神社|version=101591826|comment=Imported full ja history}} [[simple:Yodohime Shrine]] [[ja:與止日女神社]] {{Commons category|Yodohime-jinja}} [[zh:與止日女神社]] {{wikidata link|Q11613317}} [[Category:6th-century establishments in Asia]] [[Category:Buildings in Saga]] [[Category:Former Prefectural Shrines in Saga Prefecture]] [[Category:Fuken-sha]] [[Category:History of Saga]] [[Category:Hizen Province]] [[Category:Hizen Province|Shrine1]] [[Category:Ichinomiya]] [[Category:Important Cultural Property of Japan in Saga prefecture]] [[Category:Ken-sha]] [[Category:Municipal Tangible Cultural Properties in Saga Prefecture]] [[Category:Pages likely having an accidental overwite in their history that shrank them]] [[Category:Pages with merged translations]] [[Category:Shikinaisha merges]] [[Category:Pages with simple english wikipedia interwikis]] [[Category:Saga Prefecture designated tangible cultural property]] [[Category:Shikinaisha in Hizen Province]] [[Category:Shinto shrines in Saga Prefecture]] [[Category:Wikidata has short description]] [[Category:佐賀県内の市町村指定有形文化財]] [[Category:Pages with unclosed square brackets]] [[Category:Pages with unclosed curly braces]] [[Category:Junior Fifth Rank]] [[Category:Senior Fifth Rank]] [[Category:Shikinai Shōsha]] [[Category:Kokuhei-sha]] [[Category:pages]]

Senders include Seii Kokushi {{ill|Enni|en|Enni|WD=Q739826|lt=Enni}} (Saint Enni), who founded [[Tofukuji Temple]] in [[Kyoto]], and [[Imagawa Ryoshun]], the Kyushu Tandai. === Prefecture Designated === ==== Important Cultural Property ==== * West Gate - Designated on March 19, 1986{{Cite web|Japanese book|url=https://www.pref.saga.lg.jp/kiji0031451/index.html#jyu102|title=Saga Prefecture Important Cultural Property Yodohime Shrine West Gate|accessdate=2021.08.17|publisher=Saga Prefecture}}. : A [[Shikyakumon]] gate located to the northwest of the main hall, the ridge plaque copy in the Shoin documents states "Dedicated construction of the first shrine of Hizen Province Kawakami Yodohime Daimyojin West Gate by main sponsor Ryuzoji Taro Shiro Fujiwara no Ason Chikashi and Gonbu Danjo Daihitsu Takebe Nagayoshi. Constructed on an auspicious day in the third month of the fourth year of Genki (1573)". The roof is tiled, with Kirizuma-style, and the rafters are sparsely spaced. The gable has a frog decoration without carvings. The front and rear beams also have plain frog decorations, with the central bundle being rectangular. === City Designated === ==== Important Cultural Property ==== * Third Torii - Designated on October 17, 1983{{Cite web|Japanese book|url=https://www.city.saga.lg.jp/main/3887.html|title=Saga City Important Cultural Property P5|accessdate=2021.08.17|publisher=Saga City}}. : The inscription on the pillar reads "Constructed on an auspicious day in the mid-autumn of the 13th year of Keicho by Nabeshima Shinanokami Fujiwara no Ason Katsushige," indicating it was donated by Nabeshima Katsushige, the first lord of the [[Saga Domain]], in the 13th year of Keicho (1608). It is a stone Torii with a unique Hizen Torii style seen mainly in the Saga Prefecture area. Its characteristic features include three-part constructions for the Kasagi, Shimagi, Nuki, and pillars, with the Shimagi being a decorative element integrated with the Kasagi. == Others == Yodohime Shrine is designated as an Important Scenic Building in Saga City{{Cite web|Japanese book|url=https://www.city.saga.lg.jp/main/4769.html|title=Yodohime Shrine/Important Scenic Building|accessdate=2021.8.17|publisher=Saga City}}. Important Scenic Buildings in Saga City are those that have distinctive exterior features related to the region's nature, history, and culture, contributing to the formation of a favorable landscape, and are easily visible from public places such as roads{{Cite web|Japanese book|url=https://www.city.saga.lg.jp/main/333.html|title=Saga City Important Scenic Buildings|accessdate=2021.8.17|publisher=Saga City}}. == Legend == In this region, catfish are considered messengers of Yodohime-san (Yodohime-no-Mikoto) and are not eaten. Hizen Torii.]] '''Yodohime Shrine''' (Yodohime-jinja, also known as '''Yodohime Shrine''') is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en|Shinto shrine|WD=Q845945|lt=shrine}} located in {{ill|Saga Prefecture|en|Saga Prefecture|WD=Q160420|lt=Saga Prefecture}}, [[:en:Saga City|Saga City]]. It is a {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|ja|延喜式神名帳|lt=Shikinaisha}}, [[Ichinomiya]] of {{ill|Hizen Province|en|Hizen Province|WD=Q906926|lt=Hizen Province}}, and a former [[Ken-sha]] under the modern shrine Ranking system. It is also written as "Yodohime Shrine" and is also known as "'''Kawakami Shrine'''" and colloquially as "Yodohime-san." == History == === Founding === According to a fragment from the '[[Hizen Province Fudoki]]' (Shinmyocho Tochu), the god Yodohime was enshrined on November 1 in the 25th year of Emperor Kinmei (564?). It is said that Ayu fish and other fish swam upstream and dived near the northern part of Setahime Shrine, suggesting it was established as a water god worship from a river-related legend recorded in the same book'Gods of Japan' Yodohime Shrine section. === Historical Overview === In the 5th year of [[Engi (era name)|Engi]] (927), the '[[Engishiki]]' [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|Jinmyocho]] lists "Yodohime Shrine" in [[Saga District]], Hizen Province, and it was included among the {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|ja|延喜式神名帳|lt=Shikinaisha}}. In the first year of [[Kochou]] (1260), it was granted the highest Rank of Shoichii (Senior First Rank). In the {{ill|Heian period|en|Heian period|WD=Q193292|lt=Heian period}}, Tajima-no-Kami Shrine (present-day [[Tajima Shrine]]) was revered as the god of safe voyages in Hizen Province and was Ranked higher than Yodohime Shrine in the 'Jinmyocho', being the only Omiya in Hizen Province. However, after the medieval period, the actual status of Yodohime Shrine, which was closer to the provincial office, rose, and it was revered as Hizen Province's Ichinomiya. In the years of {{ill|Oho|en|Oho|WD=Q7081125|lt=Oho}} (1161-1163), it became the Ichinomiya of Hizen Province, and in the first year of Kochou (1261), it received the Shoichii Rank. However, as mentioned later, [[Chikushi Hachiman Shrine]] also claims to be Ichinomiya. During the {{ill|Mongol invasions of Japan|en|Mongol invasions of Japan|WD=Q208156|lt=Mongol invasions of Japan}} (1281), it is said that the godly spirit of Yodohime-no-Mikoto destroyed the enemy ships. In the 7th year of [[:en:Keicho|Keicho]] (1602), Emperor Go-Yozei personally bestowed a plaque inscribed with "Great Guardian of Japan's Western Region, Hizen Province's Great Protector, Shoichii Yodohime Daimyojin Ichinomiya" (preserved in the main hall: not open to the public). This confirms that Yodohime Shrine was recognized as the Ichinomiya of Hizen Province, leading to a 60-year dispute with Chikushi Hachiman Shrine over the title. According to old records, the main hall, Heiden, and Haiden were burned down in the 10th year of Bunka (1813) and rebuilt by the Nabeshima family in the 13th year of Bunka (1816). In the 4th year of [[Meiji]] (1871), it was classified as a [[Ken-sha]] under the modern shrine Ranking system. There were plans for its elevation to a Kokuheisha, but these were not realized due to the end of {{ill|Pacific War|en|Pacific War|WD=Q184425|lt=Pacific War}}. === Divine Rank === * Six National Histories ** [[Jogan (Japan)|Jogan]] 2nd year (860) February 8th, from Jugoi-no-ge to Jugoi-no-jo ( '[[Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku]]') - Written as "Yodohime Tenjin". ** Jogan 15th year (873) September 16th, Shogoi-no-ge ( 'Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku') - Written as "Yodohime no Kami". * Kochou first year (1260), Shoichii == Deities == * '''Yodohime-no-Mikoto''' *: Said to be the sister of {{ill|Empress Jingū|en|Empress Jingū|WD=Q232803|lt=Empress Jingū}}. Another theory states she is {{ill|Toyotama-hime|en|Toyotama-hime|WD=Q2329261|lt=Toyotama-hime}}Deities according to the shrine's origin story.. *: In a fragment of the '[[Hizen Province Fudoki]]' (Shinmyocho Tochu), it is stated that the alternate names for "Yodohime no Kami" are "Toyohime" and "Yodohime". Another section of the same book in Saga District includes the story of "Setahime," suggesting they are the same deity'Saga Prefecture Place names' Kawakami Shrine section.. There are many shrines dedicated to Yodohime (Yodohime no Kami) in northern Kyushu, centered around Saga Prefecture, with six of them, including this shrine, located along the [[Kase River]]. == Shrine Grounds == * First Torii (located outside the grounds) * Second Torii * Third Torii * '''Hizen Torii''': City-designated Important Cultural Property * West Gate - Prefecture-designated Important Cultural Property * Haiden, Chuden, main hall : Haiden: Five bays in front, three bays on the side, Irimoya-zukuri, Karahafu-style, with a separate Shinsenjo :Chuden: One bay in front, four bays on the side :main hall: Five-bay Nagare-zukuri, four bays on the side * Enshrined Shrine Yodohime Tenmangu The shrine grounds are located on the right bank of the [[Kase River]]. The West Gate, built in the 4th year of {{ill|Genki|en|Genki|WD=Q21501757|lt=Genki}} (1573), is a prefecture-designated Important Cultural Property, while the third Torii, built in the 13th year of [[:en:Keicho|Keicho]] (1608), is a city-designated Important Cultural Property. The first Torii stands near Tateishi Intersection ({{Coord|33|18|28.75|N|130|15|50.15|E|region:JP-41_type:landmark|name=First Torii}}). Inside the Haiden are ceiling paintings, Thirty-Six Immortal Poets plaques, and dedication plaques. The ceiling paintings consist of 250 pieces from two scrolls: "The Tale of Yamasachihiko and Umisachihiko," relating to the deity Toyotama-hime, and the "Tale of Sugawara no Michizane," related to the enshrined deity Tenmangu. The Thirty-Six Immortal Poets plaques feature portraits of renowned poets from the Heian period with one of their representative poems. The original Thirty-Six Immortal Poets plaques, which were dedicated in the late Edo period, had deteriorated and were repainted and rededicated in 2015. Both the ceiling paintings and the Thirty-Six Immortal Poets plaques were created by the painter Yin Yusheng, who resides in Saga City and is originally from [[:en:Dalian City|Dalian City]], {{ill|China|en|China|WD=Q148|lt=China}}According to local information board. Former [[Ken-sha]] |Founding = 25th year of Emperor Kinmei (564?) |main hall = Five-bay Nagare-zukuri |Alias = Kawakami Shrine, Yodohime-san |Pilgrimage = |festival = {{ill|April 18|en|April 18|WD=Q2521|lt=April 18}}, {{ill|December 18|en|December 18|WD=Q2438|lt=December 18}} |Rituals = Autumn festival (Okunchi, [[October 10]]) |map = {{location map|Japan Saga|label=Yodohime Shrine|position=bottom|width=200|float=center|caption=|mark=Shinto torii icon vermillion.svg|marksize=20}}{{maplink2|frame=yes|plain=yes|type=point|zoom=12|frame-align=center|frame-width=200}} |location = {{ill|Saga|WD=Q209766}} |coordinates = {{Coord|33.326311|N|130.268339|E|region:JP_type:landmark|display=inline,title}} }}[[File:Yodohime-jinja Haiden.jpg|thumb|right|''Yodohime jinja'']] {{nihongo|'''Yodohime jinja'''|與止日女神社|}}, also known as the '''Kawakami jinja''', is a {{ill|Japan|en|Japan|WD=Q17|lt=Japan}}ese {{ill|Shinto shrine|en|Shinto shrine|WD=Q845945|lt=Shinto shrine}} in [[:en:Saga, Saga|Saga]], {{ill|Saga Prefecture|en|Saga Prefecture|WD=Q160420|lt=Saga Prefecture}}. ==Overview== [[File:Yodohime-jinja keidai.JPG|thumb|200px|right|Shrine grounds and [[Kase River]]]] [[File:Yodohime-jinja sannnotorii.JPG|thumb|200px|right|Third Torii (City-designated cultural property)
Hizen Torii.]] '''Yodohime Shrine''' (Yodohime-jinja, also known as '''Yodohime Shrine''') is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en|Shinto shrine|WD=Q845945|lt=shrine}} located in {{ill|Saga Prefecture|en|Saga Prefecture|WD=Q160420|lt=Saga Prefecture}}, [[:en:Saga City|Saga City]]. It is a {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|ja|延喜式神名帳|lt=Shikinaisha}}, [[Ichinomiya]] of {{ill|Hizen Province|en|Hizen Province|WD=Q906926|lt=Hizen Province}}, and a former [[Ken-sha]] under the modern shrine Ranking system. It is also written as "Yodohime Shrine" and is also known as "'''Kawakami Shrine'''" and colloquially as "Yodohime-san." == History == === Founding === According to a fragment from the '[[Hizen Province Fudoki]]' (Shinmyocho Tochu), the god Yodohime was enshrined on November 1 in the 25th year of Emperor Kinmei (564?). It is said that Ayu fish and other fish swam upstream and dived near the northern part of Setahime Shrine, suggesting it was established as a water god worship from a river-related legend recorded in the same book'Gods of Japan' Yodohime Shrine section. === Historical Overview === In the 5th year of [[Engi (era name)|Engi]] (927), the '[[Engishiki]]' [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|Jinmyocho]] lists "Yodohime Shrine" in [[Saga District]], Hizen Province, and it was included among the {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|ja|延喜式神名帳|lt=Shikinaisha}}. In the first year of [[Kochou]] (1260), it was granted the highest Rank of Shoichii (Senior First Rank). In the {{ill|Heian period|en|Heian period|WD=Q193292|lt=Heian period}}, Tajima-no-Kami Shrine (present-day [[Tajima Shrine]]) was revered as the god of safe voyages in Hizen Province and was Ranked higher than Yodohime Shrine in the 'Jinmyocho', being the only Omiya in Hizen Province. However, after the medieval period, the actual status of Yodohime Shrine, which was closer to the provincial office, rose, and it was revered as Hizen Province's Ichinomiya. In the years of {{ill|Oho|en|Oho|WD=Q7081125|lt=Oho}} (1161-1163), it became the Ichinomiya of Hizen Province, and in the first year of Kochou (1261), it received the Shoichii Rank. However, as mentioned later, [[Chikushi Hachiman Shrine]] also claims to be Ichinomiya. During the {{ill|Mongol invasions of Japan|en|Mongol invasions of Japan|WD=Q208156|lt=Mongol invasions of Japan}} (1281), it is said that the godly spirit of Yodohime-no-Mikoto destroyed the enemy ships. In the 7th year of [[:en:Keicho|Keicho]] (1602), Emperor Go-Yozei personally bestowed a plaque inscribed with "Great Guardian of Japan's Western Region, Hizen Province's Great Protector, Shoichii Yodohime Daimyojin Ichinomiya" (preserved in the main hall: not open to the public). This confirms that Yodohime Shrine was recognized as the Ichinomiya of Hizen Province, leading to a 60-year dispute with Chikushi Hachiman Shrine over the title. According to old records, the main hall, Heiden, and Haiden were burned down in the 10th year of Bunka (1813) and rebuilt by the Nabeshima family in the 13th year of Bunka (1816). In the 4th year of [[Meiji]] (1871), it was classified as a [[Ken-sha]] under the modern shrine Ranking system. There were plans for its elevation to a Kokuheisha, but these were not realized due to the end of {{ill|Pacific War|en|Pacific War|WD=Q184425|lt=Pacific War}}. === Divine Rank === * Six National Histories ** [[Jogan (Japan)|Jogan]] 2nd year (860) February 8th, from Jugoi-no-ge to Jugoi-no-jo ( '[[Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku]]') - Written as "Yodohime Tenjin". ** Jogan 15th year (873) September 16th, Shogoi-no-ge ( 'Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku') - Written as "Yodohime no Kami". * Kochou first year (1260), Shoichii == Deities == * '''Yodohime-no-Mikoto''' *: Said to be the sister of {{ill|Empress Jingū|en|Empress Jingū|WD=Q232803|lt=Empress Jingū}}. Another theory states she is {{ill|Toyotama-hime|en|Toyotama-hime|WD=Q2329261|lt=Toyotama-hime}}Deities according to the shrine's origin story.. *: In a fragment of the '[[Hizen Province Fudoki]]' (Shinmyocho Tochu), it is stated that the alternate names for "Yodohime no Kami" are "Toyohime" and "Yodohime". Another section of the same book in Saga District includes the story of "Setahime," suggesting they are the same deity'Saga Prefecture Place names' Kawakami Shrine section.. There are many shrines dedicated to Yodohime (Yodohime no Kami) in northern Kyushu, centered around Saga Prefecture, with six of them, including this shrine, located along the [[Kase River]]. == Shrine Grounds == * First Torii (located outside the grounds) * Second Torii * Third Torii * '''Hizen Torii''': City-designated Important Cultural Property * West Gate - Prefecture-designated Important Cultural Property * Haiden, Chuden, main hall : Haiden: Five bays in front, three bays on the side, Irimoya-zukuri, Karahafu-style, with a separate Shinsenjo :Chuden: One bay in front, four bays on the side :main hall: Five-bay Nagare-zukuri, four bays on the side * Enshrined Shrine Yodohime Tenmangu The shrine grounds are located on the right bank of the [[Kase River]]. The West Gate, built in the 4th year of {{ill|Genki|en|Genki|WD=Q21501757|lt=Genki}} (1573), is a prefecture-designated Important Cultural Property, while the third Torii, built in the 13th year of [[:en:Keicho|Keicho]] (1608), is a city-designated Important Cultural Property. The first Torii stands near Tateishi Intersection ({{Coord|33|18|28.75|N|130|15|50.15|E|region:JP-41_type:landmark|name=First Torii}}). Inside the Haiden are ceiling paintings, Thirty-Six Immortal Poets plaques, and dedication plaques. The ceiling paintings consist of 250 pieces from two scrolls: "The Tale of Yamasachihiko and Umisachihiko," relating to the deity Toyotama-hime, and the "Tale of Sugawara no Michizane," related to the enshrined deity Tenmangu. The Thirty-Six Immortal Poets plaques feature portraits of renowned poets from the Heian period with one of their representative poems. The original Thirty-Six Immortal Poets plaques, which were dedicated in the late Edo period, had deteriorated and were repainted and rededicated in 2015. Both the ceiling paintings and the Thirty-Six Immortal Poets plaques were created by the painter Yin Yusheng, who resides in Saga City and is originally from [[:en:Dalian City|Dalian City]], {{ill|China|en|China|WD=Q148|lt=China}}According to local information board. File:Yodohime-jinja honden.JPG|main hall File:Yodohime-jinja shaden.JPG|Haiden File:Yodohime-jinja nishimon.JPG|West Gate (Prefecture-designated Cultural Property) File:Yodohime Shrine Tenman-gu.jpg|Enshrined Shrine Yodohime Tenmangu File:Yodohime-jinja ninotorii.JPG|Second Torii File:Yodohime-jinja ichinotorii.JPG|First Torii == festivals == * Spring festival (April 18) * Autumn festival (October 10) * Niiname-sai (December 18) == Cultural Properties == === Nationally Designated === ==== Important Cultural Property ==== * 14 volumes of Kawakami Shrine Documents (247 items) : 10 items from the Heian period, 92 items from the Kamakura period, 85 items from the {{ill|Nanboku-chō period|en|Nanboku-chō period|WD=Q264012|lt=Nanboku-chō period}}, 57 items from the Muromachi period, 3 items from the Azuchi-Momoyama period. Designated on June 6, 1980{{Cite web|Japanese book|url=https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/201/9051|title=Kawakami Shrine Documents (247 items)／Nationally Designated Cultural Property Database|accessdate=2021.08.17|publisher=Agency for Cultural Affairs}}. Deposited at the [[Saga Prefectural Library]]. :The oldest item among these is the Shazo Enjin Resolution from the 5th year of Kanji (1091){{Cite web|Japanese book|url=http://yodohime.area9.jp/category/0140122.html|title=Brief History of Hizen Ichinomiya Yodohime Shrine|accessdate=2021.08.17|publisher=Yodohime Shrine Official}}. These documents provide insights into the development of Ichinomiya in Kyushu, including relationships with the {{ill|Dazaifu|en|Dazaifu|WD=Q1179277|lt=Dazaifu}} and the provincial office, and the trends in Kyushu during the 14th century. Senders include Seii Kokushi {{ill|Enni|en|Enni|WD=Q739826|lt=Enni}} (Saint Enni), who founded [[Tofukuji Temple]] in {{ill|Kyoto|en|Kyoto|WD=Q34600|lt=Kyoto}}, and [[:en:Imagawa Ryoshun|Imagawa Ryoshun]], the Kyushu Tandai. === Prefecture Designated === ==== Important Cultural Property ==== * West Gate - Designated on March 19, 1986{{Cite web|Japanese book|url=https://www.pref.saga.lg.jp/kiji0031451/index.html#jyu102|title=Saga Prefecture Important Cultural Property Yodohime Shrine West Gate|accessdate=2021.08.17|publisher=Saga Prefecture}}. : A [[Shikyakumon]] gate located to the northwest of the main hall, the ridge plaque copy in the Shoin documents states "Dedicated construction of the first shrine of Hizen Province Kawakami Yodohime Daimyojin West Gate by main sponsor Ryuzoji Taro Shiro Fujiwara no Ason Chikashi and Gonbu Danjo Daihitsu Takebe Nagayoshi. Constructed on an auspicious day in the third month of the fourth year of Genki (1573)". The roof is tiled, with Kirizuma-style, and the rafters are sparsely spaced. The gable has a frog decoration without carvings. The front and rear beams also have plain frog decorations, with the central bundle being rectangular. === City Designated === ==== Important Cultural Property ==== * Third Torii - Designated on October 17, 1983{{Cite web|Japanese book|url=https://www.city.saga.lg.jp/main/3887.html|title=Saga City Important Cultural Property P5|accessdate=2021.08.17|publisher=Saga City}}. : The inscription on the pillar reads "Constructed on an auspicious day in the mid-autumn of the 13th year of Keicho by Nabeshima Shinanokami Fujiwara no Ason Katsushige," indicating it was donated by Nabeshima Katsushige, the first lord of the {{ill|Saga Domain|en|Saga Domain|WD=Q2975995|lt=Saga Domain}}, in the 13th year of Keicho (1608). It is a stone Torii with a unique Hizen Torii style seen mainly in the Saga Prefecture area. Its characteristic features include three-part constructions for the Kasagi, Shimagi, Nuki, and pillars, with the Shimagi being a decorative element integrated with the Kasagi. == Others == Yodohime Shrine is designated as an Important Scenic Building in Saga City{{Cite web|Japanese book|url=https://www.city.saga.lg.jp/main/4769.html|title=Yodohime Shrine/Important Scenic Building|accessdate=2021.8.17|publisher=Saga City}}. Important Scenic Buildings in Saga City are those that have distinctive exterior features related to the region's nature, history, and culture, contributing to the formation of a favorable landscape, and are easily visible from public places such as roads{{Cite web|Japanese book|url=https://www.city.saga.lg.jp/main/333.html|title=Saga City Important Scenic Buildings|accessdate=2021.8.17|publisher=Saga City}}. == Legend == In this region, catfish are considered messengers of Yodohime-san (Yodohime-no-Mikoto) and are not eaten. The Hizen Fudoki's section on the god of Kawakami states, "Some people who fear the fish do not suffer, while others who catch and eat it die," and it is believed that this fish corresponds to the catfish in this area. == Front Gate Sweets == * Shiratama Manju - Originates from a legend related to the shrine. == Local Information == '''location''' * {{ill|Saga Prefecture|en|Saga Prefecture|WD=Q160420|lt=Saga Prefecture}}[[:en:Saga City|Saga City]] Yamatomachi Kawakami 1 '''Access''' * From {{ill|Kyushu Railway Company|en|Kyushu Railway Company|WD=Q498366|lt=Kyushu Railway Company}} {{ill|Nagasaki Main Line|en|Nagasaki Main Line|WD=Q1078117|lt=Nagasaki Main Line}} {{ill|Saga Station|en|Saga Station|WD=Q1042665|lt=Saga Station}} ** Bus: [[Showa Bus]] to "Kawakami Bridge" bus stop (immediate walk after getting off) ** Car: About 20 minutes * Previously, there was a Hizen Kawakami Station, the terminus of the [[Saga Electric Railway]], across the Kase River. '''Nearby''' * [[Hizen Provincial Government Ruins]] * [[Funatsuka Kofun (Saga City)|Funatsuka Kofun]] - The largest keyhole-shaped Kofun in Saga Prefecture. == References == {{Reflist}} == Bibliography == * Shrine origin story * 'Japanese Historical Place names Saga Prefecture Place names' (Heibonsha) Saga District Kawakami Shrine section * [[Akira Sugitani]] 'Yodohime Shrine' (Edited by [[Kenichi Tanigawa]] 'Japanese Gods - Shrines and Sacred Sites - 1 Kyushu' (Hakusuisha)) == See also == * [[Chikushi Hachiman Shrine]] - Another shrine claiming to be Ichinomiya of Hizen Province. * [[Yodo Shrine]] * [[Tsukihi Shrine]] - A shrine in [[:en:Nara City|Nara City]] enshrining Yodohime-no-Mikoto. * [[Yoka Shrine]] - Enshrining Yodohime-no-Mikoto == External Links == {{Commonscat|Yodohime-jinja}} * [https://yodohime-jinja.jimdo.com/?logout=1/ Yodohime Shrine] (official site) * [http://www.sagabai.com/main/?cont=kanko&fid=57 Yodohime Shrine] (Saga City Tourism Association) {{Shinto shrines}} ==History== ''Yodohime jinja'' was founded in the sixth century. It enshrines the ''[[kami]]'' of the grandmother of {{ill|Emperor Jimmu|en|Emperor Jimmu|WD=Q200188|lt=Emperor Jimmu}}. It was one of two chief {{ill|Shinto shrine|en|Shinto shrine|WD=Q845945|lt=Shinto shrine}} (''[[ichinomiya]]'') of {{ill|Hizen Province|en|Hizen Province|WD=Q906926|lt=Hizen Province}} and Saga Prefecture.Picken, Stuart. (2004). There are many shrines dedicated to Yodohime (Yodohime no Kami) in northern Kyushu, centered around Saga Prefecture, with six of them, including this shrine, located along the [[Kase River]]. == Shrine Grounds == * First Torii (located outside the grounds) * Second Torii * Third Torii * '''Hizen Torii''': City-designated Important Cultural Property * West Gate - Prefecture-designated Important Cultural Property * Haiden, Chuden, main hall : Haiden: Five bays in front, three bays on the side, Irimoya-zukuri, Karahafu-style, with a separate Shinsenjo :Chuden: One bay in front, four bays on the side :main hall: Five-bay Nagare-zukuri, four bays on the side * Enshrined Shrine Yodohime Tenmangu The shrine grounds are located on the right bank of the [[Kase River]]. The West Gate, built in the 4th year of {{ill|Genki|en|Genki|WD=Q21501757|lt=Genki}} (1573), is a prefecture-designated Important Cultural Property, while the third Torii, built in the 13th year of [[Keicho]] (1608), is a city-designated Important Cultural Property. The first Torii stands near Tateishi Intersection ({{Coord|33|18|28.75|N|130|15|50.15|E|region:JP-41_type:landmark|name=First Torii}}). Inside the Haiden are ceiling paintings, Thirty-Six Immortal Poets plaques, and dedication plaques. The ceiling paintings consist of 250 pieces from two scrolls: "The Tale of Yamasachihiko and Umisachihiko," relating to the deity Toyotama-hime, and the "Tale of Sugawara no Michizane," related to the enshrined deity Tenmangu. Hizen Torii.]] '''Yodohime Shrine''' (Yodohime-jinja, also known as '''Yodohime Shrine''') is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en|Shinto shrine|WD=Q845945|lt=shrine}} located in {{ill|Saga Prefecture|en|Saga Prefecture|WD=Q160420|lt=Saga Prefecture}}, [[:en:Saga City|Saga City]]. It is a {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|ja|延喜式神名帳|lt=Shikinaisha}}, [[Ichinomiya]] of {{ill|Hizen Province|en|Hizen Province|WD=Q906926|lt=Hizen Province}}, and a former [[Ken-sha]] under the modern shrine Ranking system. It is also written as "Yodohime Shrine" and is also known as "'''Kawakami Shrine'''" and colloquially as "Yodohime-san." == History == === Founding === According to a fragment from the '[[Hizen Province Fudoki]]' (Shinmyocho Tochu), the god Yodohime was enshrined on November 1 in the 25th year of Emperor Kinmei (564?). It is said that Ayu fish and other fish swam upstream and dived near the northern part of Setahime Shrine, suggesting it was established as a water god worship from a river-related legend recorded in the same book'Gods of Japan' Yodohime Shrine section. === Historical Overview === In the 5th year of [[Engi (era name)|Engi]] (927), the '[[Engishiki]]' [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|Jinmyocho]] lists "Yodohime Shrine" in [[Saga District]], Hizen Province, and it was included among the {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|ja|延喜式神名帳|lt=Shikinaisha}}. In the first year of [[Kochou]] (1260), it was granted the highest Rank of Shoichii (Senior First Rank). In the {{ill|Heian period|en|Heian period|WD=Q193292|lt=Heian period}}, Tajima-no-Kami Shrine (present-day [[Tajima Shrine]]) was revered as the god of safe voyages in Hizen Province and was Ranked higher than Yodohime Shrine in the 'Jinmyocho', being the only Omiya in Hizen Province. However, after the medieval period, the actual status of Yodohime Shrine, which was closer to the provincial office, rose, and it was revered as Hizen Province's Ichinomiya. In the years of {{ill|Oho|en|Oho|WD=Q7081125|lt=Oho}} (1161-1163), it became the Ichinomiya of Hizen Province, and in the first year of Kochou (1261), it received the Shoichii Rank. However, as mentioned later, [[Chikushi Hachiman Shrine]] also claims to be Ichinomiya. During the {{ill|Mongol invasions of Japan|en|Mongol invasions of Japan|WD=Q208156|lt=Mongol invasions of Japan}} (1281), it is said that the godly spirit of Yodohime-no-Mikoto destroyed the enemy ships. In the 7th year of [[:en:Keicho|Keicho]] (1602), Emperor Go-Yozei personally bestowed a plaque inscribed with "Great Guardian of Japan's Western Region, Hizen Province's Great Protector, Shoichii Yodohime Daimyojin Ichinomiya" (preserved in the main hall: not open to the public). This confirms that Yodohime Shrine was recognized as the Ichinomiya of Hizen Province, leading to a 60-year dispute with Chikushi Hachiman Shrine over the title. According to old records, the main hall, Heiden, and Haiden were burned down in the 10th year of Bunka (1813) and rebuilt by the Nabeshima family in the 13th year of Bunka (1816). In the 4th year of [[Meiji]] (1871), it was classified as a [[Ken-sha]] under the modern shrine Ranking system. There were plans for its elevation to a Kokuheisha, but these were not realized due to the end of {{ill|Pacific War|en|Pacific War|WD=Q184425|lt=Pacific War}}. === Divine Rank === * Six National Histories ** [[Jogan (Japan)|Jogan]] 2nd year (860) February 8th, from Jugoi-no-ge to Jugoi-no-jo ( '[[Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku]]') - Written as "Yodohime Tenjin". ** Jogan 15th year (873) September 16th, Shogoi-no-ge ( 'Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku') - Written as "Yodohime no Kami". * Kochou first year (1260), Shoichii == Deities == * '''Yodohime-no-Mikoto''' *: Said to be the sister of {{ill|Empress Jingū|en|Empress Jingū|WD=Q232803|lt=Empress Jingū}}. Former [[Ken-sha]] |Founding = 25th year of Emperor Kinmei (564?) |main hall = Five-bay Nagare-zukuri |Alias = Kawakami Shrine, Yodohime-san |Pilgrimage = |festival = {{ill|April 18|en|April 18|WD=Q2521|lt=April 18}}, {{ill|December 18|en|December 18|WD=Q2438|lt=December 18}} |Rituals = Autumn festival (Okunchi, [[October 10]]) |map = {{location map|Japan Saga|label=Yodohime Shrine|position=bottom|width=200|float=center|caption=|mark=Shinto torii icon vermillion.svg|marksize=20}}{{maplink2|frame=yes|plain=yes|type=point|zoom=12|frame-align=center|frame-width=200}} |location = {{ill|Saga|WD=Q209766}} |coordinates = {{Coord|33.326311|N|130.268339|E|region:JP_type:landmark|display=inline,title}} }}[[File:Yodohime-jinja Haiden.jpg|thumb|right|''Yodohime jinja'']] {{nihongo|'''Yodohime jinja'''|與止日女神社|}}, also known as the '''Kawakami jinja''', is a {{ill|Japan|en|Japan|WD=Q17|lt=Japan}}ese {{ill|Shinto shrine|en|Shinto shrine|WD=Q845945|lt=Shinto shrine}} in [[:en:Saga, Saga|Saga]], {{ill|Saga Prefecture|en|Saga Prefecture|WD=Q160420|lt=Saga Prefecture}}. ==Overview== [[File:Yodohime-jinja keidai.JPG|thumb|200px|right|Shrine grounds and [[Kase River]]]] [[File:Yodohime-jinja sannnotorii.JPG|thumb|200px|right|Third Torii (City-designated cultural property)
Hizen Torii.]] '''Yodohime Shrine''' (Yodohime-jinja, also known as '''Yodohime Shrine''') is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en|Shinto shrine|WD=Q845945|lt=shrine}} located in {{ill|Saga Prefecture|en|Saga Prefecture|WD=Q160420|lt=Saga Prefecture}}, [[:en:Saga City|Saga City]]. It is a {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|ja|延喜式神名帳|lt=Shikinaisha}}, [[Ichinomiya]] of {{ill|Hizen Province|en|Hizen Province|WD=Q906926|lt=Hizen Province}}, and a former [[Ken-sha]] under the modern shrine Ranking system. It is also written as "Yodohime Shrine" and is also known as "'''Kawakami Shrine'''" and colloquially as "Yodohime-san." == History == === Founding === According to a fragment from the '[[Hizen Province Fudoki]]' (Shinmyocho Tochu), the god Yodohime was enshrined on November 1 in the 25th year of Emperor Kinmei (564?). It is said that Ayu fish and other fish swam upstream and dived near the northern part of Setahime Shrine, suggesting it was established as a water god worship from a river-related legend recorded in the same book'Gods of Japan' Yodohime Shrine section. === Historical Overview === In the 5th year of [[Engi (era name)|Engi]] (927), the '[[Engishiki]]' [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|Jinmyocho]] lists "Yodohime Shrine" in [[Saga District]], Hizen Province, and it was included among the {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|ja|延喜式神名帳|lt=Shikinaisha}}. In the first year of [[Kochou]] (1260), it was granted the highest Rank of Shoichii (Senior First Rank). In the {{ill|Heian period|en|Heian period|WD=Q193292|lt=Heian period}}, Tajima-no-Kami Shrine (present-day [[Tajima Shrine]]) was revered as the god of safe voyages in Hizen Province and was Ranked higher than Yodohime Shrine in the 'Jinmyocho', being the only Omiya in Hizen Province. However, after the medieval period, the actual status of Yodohime Shrine, which was closer to the provincial office, rose, and it was revered as Hizen Province's Ichinomiya. In the years of {{ill|Oho|en|Oho|WD=Q7081125|lt=Oho}} (1161-1163), it became the Ichinomiya of Hizen Province, and in the first year of Kochou (1261), it received the Shoichii Rank. However, as mentioned later, [[Chikushi Hachiman Shrine]] also claims to be Ichinomiya. During the {{ill|Mongol invasions of Japan|en|Mongol invasions of Japan|WD=Q208156|lt=Mongol invasions of Japan}} (1281), it is said that the godly spirit of Yodohime-no-Mikoto destroyed the enemy ships. In the 7th year of [[:en:Keicho|Keicho]] (1602), Emperor Go-Yozei personally bestowed a plaque inscribed with "Great Guardian of Japan's Western Region, Hizen Province's Great Protector, Shoichii Yodohime Daimyojin Ichinomiya" (preserved in the main hall: not open to the public). This confirms that Yodohime Shrine was recognized as the Ichinomiya of Hizen Province, leading to a 60-year dispute with Chikushi Hachiman Shrine over the title. According to old records, the main hall, Heiden, and Haiden were burned down in the 10th year of Bunka (1813) and rebuilt by the Nabeshima family in the 13th year of Bunka (1816). In the 4th year of [[Meiji]] (1871), it was classified as a [[Ken-sha]] under the modern shrine Ranking system. There were plans for its elevation to a Kokuheisha, but these were not realized due to the end of {{ill|Pacific War|en|Pacific War|WD=Q184425|lt=Pacific War}}. === Divine Rank === * Six National Histories ** [[Jogan (Japan)|Jogan]] 2nd year (860) February 8th, from Jugoi-no-ge to Jugoi-no-jo ( '[[Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku]]') - Written as "Yodohime Tenjin". ** Jogan 15th year (873) September 16th, Shogoi-no-ge ( 'Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku') - Written as "Yodohime no Kami". * Kochou first year (1260), Shoichii == Deities == * '''Yodohime-no-Mikoto''' *: Said to be the sister of {{ill|Empress Jingū|en|Empress Jingū|WD=Q232803|lt=Empress Jingū}}. Another theory states she is {{ill|Toyotama-hime|en|Toyotama-hime|WD=Q2329261|lt=Toyotama-hime}}Deities according to the shrine's origin story.. *: In a fragment of the '[[Hizen Province Fudoki]]' (Shinmyocho Tochu), it is stated that the alternate names for "Yodohime no Kami" are "Toyohime" and "Yodohime". Another section of the same book in Saga District includes the story of "Setahime," suggesting they are the same deity'Saga Prefecture Place names' Kawakami Shrine section.. There are many shrines dedicated to Yodohime (Yodohime no Kami) in northern Kyushu, centered around Saga Prefecture, with six of them, including this shrine, located along the [[Kase River]]. == Shrine Grounds == * First Torii (located outside the grounds) * Second Torii * Third Torii * '''Hizen Torii''': City-designated Important Cultural Property * West Gate - Prefecture-designated Important Cultural Property * Haiden, Chuden, main hall : Haiden: Five bays in front, three bays on the side, Irimoya-zukuri, Karahafu-style, with a separate Shinsenjo :Chuden: One bay in front, four bays on the side :main hall: Five-bay Nagare-zukuri, four bays on the side * Enshrined Shrine Yodohime Tenmangu The shrine grounds are located on the right bank of the [[Kase River]]. The West Gate, built in the 4th year of {{ill|Genki|en|Genki|WD=Q21501757|lt=Genki}} (1573), is a prefecture-designated Important Cultural Property, while the third Torii, built in the 13th year of [[:en:Keicho|Keicho]] (1608), is a city-designated Important Cultural Property. The first Torii stands near Tateishi Intersection ({{Coord|33|18|28.75|N|130|15|50.15|E|region:JP-41_type:landmark|name=First Torii}}). Inside the Haiden are ceiling paintings, Thirty-Six Immortal Poets plaques, and dedication plaques. The ceiling paintings consist of 250 pieces from two scrolls: "The Tale of Yamasachihiko and Umisachihiko," relating to the deity Toyotama-hime, and the "Tale of Sugawara no Michizane," related to the enshrined deity Tenmangu. The Thirty-Six Immortal Poets plaques feature portraits of renowned poets from the Heian period with one of their representative poems. The original Thirty-Six Immortal Poets plaques, which were dedicated in the late Edo period, had deteriorated and were repainted and rededicated in 2015. Both the ceiling paintings and the Thirty-Six Immortal Poets plaques were created by the painter Yin Yusheng, who resides in Saga City and is originally from [[:en:Dalian City|Dalian City]], {{ill|China|en|China|WD=Q148|lt=China}}According to local information board. File:Yodohime-jinja honden.JPG|main hall File:Yodohime-jinja shaden.JPG|Haiden File:Yodohime-jinja nishimon.JPG|West Gate (Prefecture-designated Cultural Property) File:Yodohime Shrine Tenman-gu.jpg|Enshrined Shrine Yodohime Tenmangu File:Yodohime-jinja ninotorii.JPG|Second Torii File:Yodohime-jinja ichinotorii.JPG|First Torii == festivals == * Spring festival (April 18) * Autumn festival (October 10) * Niiname-sai (December 18) == Cultural Properties == === Nationally Designated === ==== Important Cultural Property ==== * 14 volumes of Kawakami Shrine Documents (247 items) : 10 items from the Heian period, 92 items from the Kamakura period, 85 items from the {{ill|Nanboku-chō period|en|Nanboku-chō period|WD=Q264012|lt=Nanboku-chō period}}, 57 items from the Muromachi period, 3 items from the Azuchi-Momoyama period. Designated on June 6, 1980{{Cite web|Japanese book|url=https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/201/9051|title=Kawakami Shrine Documents (247 items)／Nationally Designated Cultural Property Database|accessdate=2021.08.17|publisher=Agency for Cultural Affairs}}. Deposited at the [[Saga Prefectural Library]]. :The oldest item among these is the Shazo Enjin Resolution from the 5th year of Kanji (1091){{Cite web|Japanese book|url=http://yodohime.area9.jp/category/0140122.html|title=Brief History of Hizen Ichinomiya Yodohime Shrine|accessdate=2021.08.17|publisher=Yodohime Shrine Official}}. These documents provide insights into the development of Ichinomiya in Kyushu, including relationships with the {{ill|Dazaifu|en|Dazaifu|WD=Q1179277|lt=Dazaifu}} and the provincial office, and the trends in Kyushu during the 14th century. Senders include Seii Kokushi {{ill|Enni|en|Enni|WD=Q739826|lt=Enni}} (Saint Enni), who founded [[Tofukuji Temple]] in {{ill|Kyoto|en|Kyoto|WD=Q34600|lt=Kyoto}}, and [[:en:Imagawa Ryoshun|Imagawa Ryoshun]], the Kyushu Tandai. === Prefecture Designated === ==== Important Cultural Property ==== * West Gate - Designated on March 19, 1986{{Cite web|Japanese book|url=https://www.pref.saga.lg.jp/kiji0031451/index.html#jyu102|title=Saga Prefecture Important Cultural Property Yodohime Shrine West Gate|accessdate=2021.08.17|publisher=Saga Prefecture}}. : A [[Shikyakumon]] gate located to the northwest of the main hall, the ridge plaque copy in the Shoin documents states "Dedicated construction of the first shrine of Hizen Province Kawakami Yodohime Daimyojin West Gate by main sponsor Ryuzoji Taro Shiro Fujiwara no Ason Chikashi and Gonbu Danjo Daihitsu Takebe Nagayoshi. Constructed on an auspicious day in the third month of the fourth year of Genki (1573)". The roof is tiled, with Kirizuma-style, and the rafters are sparsely spaced. The gable has a frog decoration without carvings. The front and rear beams also have plain frog decorations, with the central bundle being rectangular. === City Designated === ==== Important Cultural Property ==== * Third Torii - Designated on October 17, 1983{{Cite web|Japanese book|url=https://www.city.saga.lg.jp/main/3887.html|title=Saga City Important Cultural Property P5|accessdate=2021.08.17|publisher=Saga City}}. : The inscription on the pillar reads "Constructed on an auspicious day in the mid-autumn of the 13th year of Keicho by Nabeshima Shinanokami Fujiwara no Ason Katsushige," indicating it was donated by Nabeshima Katsushige, the first lord of the {{ill|Saga Domain|en|Saga Domain|WD=Q2975995|lt=Saga Domain}}, in the 13th year of Keicho (1608). It is a stone Torii with a unique Hizen Torii style seen mainly in the Saga Prefecture area. Its characteristic features include three-part constructions for the Kasagi, Shimagi, Nuki, and pillars, with the Shimagi being a decorative element integrated with the Kasagi. == Others == Yodohime Shrine is designated as an Important Scenic Building in Saga City{{Cite web|Japanese book|url=https://www.city.saga.lg.jp/main/4769.html|title=Yodohime Shrine/Important Scenic Building|accessdate=2021.8.17|publisher=Saga City}}. Important Scenic Buildings in Saga City are those that have distinctive exterior features related to the region's nature, history, and culture, contributing to the formation of a favorable landscape, and are easily visible from public places such as roads{{Cite web|Japanese book|url=https://www.city.saga.lg.jp/main/333.html|title=Saga City Important Scenic Buildings|accessdate=2021.8.17|publisher=Saga City}}. == Legend == In this region, catfish are considered messengers of Yodohime-san (Yodohime-no-Mikoto) and are not eaten. The Hizen Fudoki's section on the god of Kawakami states, "Some people who fear the fish do not suffer, while others who catch and eat it die," and it is believed that this fish corresponds to the catfish in this area. == Front Gate Sweets == * Shiratama Manju - Originates from a legend related to the shrine. == Local Information == '''location''' * {{ill|Saga Prefecture|en|Saga Prefecture|WD=Q160420|lt=Saga Prefecture}}[[:en:Saga City|Saga City]] Yamatomachi Kawakami 1 '''Access''' * From {{ill|Kyushu Railway Company|en|Kyushu Railway Company|WD=Q498366|lt=Kyushu Railway Company}} {{ill|Nagasaki Main Line|en|Nagasaki Main Line|WD=Q1078117|lt=Nagasaki Main Line}} {{ill|Saga Station|en|Saga Station|WD=Q1042665|lt=Saga Station}} ** Bus: [[Showa Bus]] to "Kawakami Bridge" bus stop (immediate walk after getting off) ** Car: About 20 minutes * Previously, there was a Hizen Kawakami Station, the terminus of the [[Saga Electric Railway]], across the Kase River. '''Nearby''' * [[Hizen Provincial Government Ruins]] * [[Funatsuka Kofun (Saga City)|Funatsuka Kofun]] - The largest keyhole-shaped Kofun in Saga Prefecture. == References == {{Reflist}} == Bibliography == * Shrine origin story * 'Japanese Historical Place names Saga Prefecture Place names' (Heibonsha) Saga District Kawakami Shrine section * [[Akira Sugitani]] 'Yodohime Shrine' (Edited by [[Kenichi Tanigawa]] 'Japanese Gods - Shrines and Sacred Sites - 1 Kyushu' (Hakusuisha)) == See also == * [[Chikushi Hachiman Shrine]] - Another shrine claiming to be Ichinomiya of Hizen Province. * [[Yodo Shrine]] * [[Tsukihi Shrine]] - A shrine in [[:en:Nara City|Nara City]] enshrining Yodohime-no-Mikoto. * [[Yoka Shrine]] - Enshrining Yodohime-no-Mikoto == External Links == {{Commonscat|Yodohime-jinja}} * [https://yodohime-jinja.jimdo.com/?logout=1/ Yodohime Shrine] (official site) * [http://www.sagabai.com/main/?cont=kanko&fid=57 Yodohime Shrine] (Saga City Tourism Association) {{Shinto shrines}} ==History== ''Yodohime jinja'' was founded in the sixth century. This confirms that Yodohime Shrine was recognized as the Ichinomiya of Hizen Province, leading to a 60-year dispute with Chikushi Hachiman Shrine over the title. According to old records, the main hall, Heiden, and Haiden were burned down in the 10th year of Bunka (1813) and rebuilt by the Nabeshima family in the 13th year of Bunka (1816). In the 4th year of [[Meiji]] (1871), it was classified as a [[Ken-sha]] under the modern shrine Ranking system. There are many shrines dedicated to Yodohime (Yodohime no Kami) in northern Kyushu, centered around Saga Prefecture, with six of them, including this shrine, located along the [[Kase River]]. == Shrine Grounds == * First Torii (located outside the grounds) * Second Torii * Third Torii * '''Hizen Torii''': City-designated Important Cultural Property * West Gate - Prefecture-designated Important Cultural Property * Haiden, Chuden, main hall : Haiden: Five bays in front, three bays on the side, Irimoya-zukuri, Karahafu-style, with a separate Shinsenjo :Chuden: One bay in front, four bays on the side :main hall: Five-bay Nagare-zukuri, four bays on the side * Enshrined Shrine Yodohime Tenmangu The shrine grounds are located on the right bank of the [[Kase River]]. The West Gate, built in the 4th year of {{ill|Genki|en|Genki|WD=Q21501757|lt=Genki}} (1573), is a prefecture-designated Important Cultural Property, while the third Torii, built in the 13th year of [[Keicho]] (1608), is a city-designated Important Cultural Property. The first Torii stands near Tateishi Intersection ({{Coord|33|18|28.75|N|130|15|50.15|E|region:JP-41_type:landmark|name=First Torii}}). Inside the Haiden are ceiling paintings, Thirty-Six Immortal Poets plaques, and dedication plaques. The ceiling paintings consist of 250 pieces from two scrolls: "The Tale of Yamasachihiko and Umisachihiko," relating to the deity Toyotama-hime, and the "Tale of Sugawara no Michizane," related to the enshrined deity Tenmangu. The Thirty-Six Immortal Poets plaques feature portraits of renowned poets from the Heian period with one of their representative poems. The original Thirty-Six Immortal Poets plaques, which were dedicated in the late Edo period, had deteriorated and were repainted and rededicated in 2015. The gable has a frog decoration without carvings. The front and rear beams also have plain frog decorations, with the central bundle being rectangular. === City Designated === ==== Important Cultural Property ==== * Third Torii - Designated on October 17, 1983{{Cite web|Japanese book|url=https://www.city.saga.lg.jp/main/3887.html|title=Saga City Important Cultural Property P5|accessdate=2021.08.17|publisher=Saga City}}. : The inscription on the pillar reads "Constructed on an auspicious day in the mid-autumn of the 13th year of Keicho by Nabeshima Shinanokami Fujiwara no Ason Katsushige," indicating it was donated by Nabeshima Katsushige, the first lord of the [[Saga Domain]], in the 13th year of Keicho (1608). It is a stone Torii with a unique Hizen Torii style seen mainly in the Saga Prefecture area. Its characteristic features include three-part constructions for the Kasagi, Shimagi, Nuki, and pillars, with the Shimagi being a decorative element integrated with the Kasagi. == Others == Yodohime Shrine is designated as an Important Scenic Building in Saga City{{Cite web|Japanese book|url=https://www.city.saga.lg.jp/main/4769.html|title=Yodohime Shrine/Important Scenic Building|accessdate=2021.8.17|publisher=Saga City}}. Important Scenic Buildings in Saga City are those that have distinctive exterior features related to the region's nature, history, and culture, contributing to the formation of a favorable landscape, and are easily visible from public places such as roads{{Cite web|Japanese book|url=https://www.city.saga.lg.jp/main/333.html|title=Saga City Important Scenic Buildings|accessdate=2021.8.17|publisher=Saga City}}. == Legend == In this region, catfish are considered messengers of Yodohime-san (Yodohime-no-Mikoto) and are not eaten. Hizen Torii.]] '''Yodohime Shrine''' (Yodohime-jinja, also known as '''Yodohime Shrine''') is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en|Shinto shrine|WD=Q845945|lt=shrine}} located in {{ill|Saga Prefecture|en|Saga Prefecture|WD=Q160420|lt=Saga Prefecture}}, [[:en:Saga City|Saga City]]. It is a {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|ja|延喜式神名帳|lt=Shikinaisha}}, [[Ichinomiya]] of {{ill|Hizen Province|en|Hizen Province|WD=Q906926|lt=Hizen Province}}, and a former [[Ken-sha]] under the modern shrine Ranking system. It is also written as "Yodohime Shrine" and is also known as "'''Kawakami Shrine'''" and colloquially as "Yodohime-san." == History == === Founding === According to a fragment from the '[[Hizen Province Fudoki]]' (Shinmyocho Tochu), the god Yodohime was enshrined on November 1 in the 25th year of Emperor Kinmei (564?). It is said that Ayu fish and other fish swam upstream and dived near the northern part of Setahime Shrine, suggesting it was established as a water god worship from a river-related legend recorded in the same book'Gods of Japan' Yodohime Shrine section. === Historical Overview === In the 5th year of [[Engi (era name)|Engi]] (927), the '[[Engishiki]]' [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|Jinmyocho]] lists "Yodohime Shrine" in [[Saga District]], Hizen Province, and it was included among the {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|ja|延喜式神名帳|lt=Shikinaisha}}. In the first year of [[Kochou]] (1260), it was granted the highest Rank of Shoichii (Senior First Rank). In the {{ill|Heian period|en|Heian period|WD=Q193292|lt=Heian period}}, Tajima-no-Kami Shrine (present-day [[Tajima Shrine]]) was revered as the god of safe voyages in Hizen Province and was Ranked higher than Yodohime Shrine in the 'Jinmyocho', being the only Omiya in Hizen Province. However, after the medieval period, the actual status of Yodohime Shrine, which was closer to the provincial office, rose, and it was revered as Hizen Province's Ichinomiya. In the years of {{ill|Oho|en|Oho|WD=Q7081125|lt=Oho}} (1161-1163), it became the Ichinomiya of Hizen Province, and in the first year of Kochou (1261), it received the Shoichii Rank. However, as mentioned later, [[Chikushi Hachiman Shrine]] also claims to be Ichinomiya. During the {{ill|Mongol invasions of Japan|en|Mongol invasions of Japan|WD=Q208156|lt=Mongol invasions of Japan}} (1281), it is said that the godly spirit of Yodohime-no-Mikoto destroyed the enemy ships. The Hizen Fudoki's section on the god of Kawakami states, "Some people who fear the fish do not suffer, while others who catch and eat it die," and it is believed that this fish corresponds to the catfish in this area. == Front Gate Sweets == * Shiratama Manju - Originates from a legend related to the shrine. == Local Information == '''location''' * {{ill|Saga Prefecture|en|Saga Prefecture|WD=Q160420|lt=Saga Prefecture}}[[:en:Saga City|Saga City]] Yamatomachi Kawakami 1 '''Access''' * From {{ill|Kyushu Railway Company|en|Kyushu Railway Company|WD=Q498366|lt=Kyushu Railway Company}} {{ill|Nagasaki Main Line|en|Nagasaki Main Line|WD=Q1078117|lt=Nagasaki Main Line}} {{ill|Saga Station|en|Saga Station|WD=Q1042665|lt=Saga Station}} ** Bus: [[Showa Bus]] to "Kawakami Bridge" bus stop (immediate walk after getting off) ** Car: About 20 minutes * Previously, there was a Hizen Kawakami Station, the terminus of the [[Saga Electric Railway]], across the Kase River.
